# TrafficSchoolPicker.com — Full State Reference

> Structured facts for every US state (and Washington DC) traffic school program.
> Source: TrafficSchoolPicker per-state editorial content, verified against official DMV and court records.
> Auto-generated at build time from the States content database.

## Alabama

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/alabama

Alabama has no statewide traffic-school program that automatically dismisses a ticket. Whether a course helps depends on the court on your citation: some municipal courts allow an approved course toward a dismissal at the judge's discretion, so confirm with that court before you enroll. State law does provide one clear course benefit, an auto-insurance premium reduction for drivers age 55 and older who complete an approved accident-prevention course of at least six hours, which can be taken in a classroom or online (Ala. Code §§ 27-13-120 to 27-13-121). Last checked August 2026.

**Source:** Ala. Code § 27-13-120 (premium reduction); Ala. Code § 27-13-121 (approved courses)

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Does an online traffic school dismiss a ticket in Alabama?**
There is no statewide program that does. Some Alabama municipal courts allow an approved course toward a dismissal at the judge's discretion, so confirm with the court printed on your citation before you enroll.

**Can a course lower my Alabama insurance?**
Yes. Drivers age 55 and older who complete an approved accident-prevention course of at least six hours, in a classroom or online, qualify for a mandated auto-insurance premium reduction (Ala. Code §§ 27-13-120 to 27-13-121).

**Who approves the course in Alabama?**
For the insurance discount, the course must be sponsored by the National Safety Council, AAA, or AARP, or be an equivalent course approved by the Department of Public Safety (Ala. Code § 27-13-121).

## Alaska

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/alaska

Alaska does not dismiss most tickets through traffic school, but the Alaska DMV does offer a point reduction: completing an approved defensive driving course reduces points on your driving record, once every 12 months. Alaska publishes a list of approved courses but no set course length. It reduces points rather than dismissing the ticket, and any actual dismissal is up to the court on your citation. Last checked August 2026.

**Source:** Alaska DMV Points and approved driving schools (dmv.alaska.gov/driver-services-adjudication/points/)

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Does an online course dismiss a ticket in Alaska?**
No. Alaska's statewide benefit is a point reduction: completing an approved defensive driving course reduces points on your record, once every 12 months. Any actual ticket dismissal is separate and decided by the court on your citation.

**How often can I use the Alaska point reduction?**
Once every 12 months, for completing an Alaska DMV-approved defensive driving course (Alaska DMV Points). Confirm the current course list and rules with the Alaska DMV before you enroll.

**How long is the Alaska course?**
Alaska publishes a list of approved defensive driving courses but does not set a single statewide course length, so length varies by provider. Check the provider before you pay.

---

## Arizona

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/arizona

Arizona drivers cited for a civil moving violation can complete a Defensive Driving School (DDS) course of 240 to 270 minutes (4 to 4.5 hours) under ACJA § 7-205 and A.R.S. §§ 28-3391 to 28-3399 to dismiss the ticket and keep points off the MVD record. The Arizona Supreme Court regulates the DDS program; eligible drivers can use it once every 12 months from violation date to violation date, must complete the course at least seven days before the scheduled court date, and may dismiss only one violation per citation. CDL holders and drivers cited in commercial vehicles are excluded, as are violations involving a serious-injury or fatal accident and most criminal violations. The all-in cost is the school's course fee plus a court diversion fee that varies by court (Maricopa County roughly $110 to $162), a $24 State Fee, and a $45 state surcharge. DDS is distinct from Traffic Survival School (TSS), the separate 8-hour MVD-mandated remediation course required after certain serious offenses or point accumulation; TSS does not dismiss tickets. Last checked August 2026.

**Source:** ACJA § 7-205(E)(1)(k) (Arizona Supreme Court Defensive Driving School)

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Estimated all-in cost of a first speeding ticket:** $3,270 (fine plus a three-year insurance surcharge; 2026 study at https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket)

**Does Arizona defensive driving dismiss my ticket?**
Yes. Completing an Arizona Supreme Court-approved Defensive Driving School (DDS) course dismisses an eligible civil traffic ticket and keeps points off your MVD record (A.R.S. § 28-3392). It is one of the more complete dismissal programs in the country.

**How long is Arizona defensive driving?**
A DDS course is 240 to 270 minutes, about 4 to 4.5 hours (ACJA § 7-205). Do not confuse it with the 8-hour Traffic Survival School (TSS), a separate MVD remediation course that does not dismiss tickets.

**How often can I use Arizona defensive driving?**
Once every 12 months, measured violation date to violation date (A.R.S. § 28-3392(B)). You can dismiss only one violation per citation, and you must finish the course at least seven days before your court date.

**Who submits my certificate in Arizona?**
The school does. Your Supreme Court-approved school reports your completion to the court electronically, so you do not mail anything yourself. Keep a copy for your records.

**Can I do Arizona defensive driving online?**
Yes. Arizona Supreme Court-approved online DDS courses are accepted statewide. Confirm your provider is on the Supreme Court's approved-school list at azcourts.gov/drive before enrolling.

## Arkansas

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/arkansas

Arkansas has no statewide traffic-school program that automatically dismisses a ticket. Whether a course helps is up to the court on your citation, so confirm with that court before enrolling. State law does provide an insurance benefit for older drivers: under Ark. Code § 27-19-608, drivers age 55 and older who complete an approved accident-prevention course get an auto-insurance premium reduction for three years. Note that Arkansas requires this mature-driver course to be taken in a classroom, not online. Last checked August 2026.

**Source:** Ark. Code § 27-19-608

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Does an online traffic school dismiss a ticket in Arkansas?**
There is no statewide program that does. Whether an approved course helps with your ticket is decided by the court on your citation, so confirm with that court before you enroll.

**Can a course lower my Arkansas insurance?**
Yes, for older drivers. Under Ark. Code § 27-19-608, drivers age 55 and older who complete an approved accident-prevention course get an auto-insurance premium reduction for three years, and must retake the course every three years to keep it.

**Can I take the Arkansas mature-driver course online?**
No. Arkansas requires the mature-driver accident-prevention course tied to the insurance discount to be completed in a classroom, not online. Confirm approved providers with the Arkansas Office of Driver Services.

---

## California

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/california

California drivers cited for an eligible one-point moving violation can complete a state-licensed 8-hour Traffic Violator School (TVS) course to hold the conviction confidential under Vehicle Code § 1808.7: insurers do not see it and no point is assessed. There is no expiry on that confidentiality. What the 18 months controls is frequency: you can use traffic school once per 18-month period, measured violation date to violation date. The option requires an eligible violation and a valid non-commercial license, and excludes violations 25-plus mph over the limit, alcohol- or drug-related offenses, and any offense in a commercial vehicle regardless of license class. The court charges an administrative fee, set by each county court and typically about $50 to $70 (Butte $52, Los Angeles $64), plus the TVS provider's course fee. Last checked August 2026.

**Source:** California DMV Traffic Violator School program standard (dmv.ca.gov)

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Estimated all-in cost of a first speeding ticket:** $5,619 (fine plus a three-year insurance surcharge; 2026 study at https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket)

**Who submits my certificate to the California court?**
Your school submits the certificate electronically to the DMV and court on your behalf. You do not need to mail anything — but confirm the school offers electronic submission before enrolling, as some older schools still require you to handle it yourself.

**How often can I do California traffic school?**
Once every 18 months. The 18-month period is calculated from the date of the violation for which you last used traffic school, not the completion date. If you receive another eligible ticket within 18 months, you cannot use traffic school for that ticket.

**Can I complete California traffic school online?**
Yes. California courts accept DMV-licensed online traffic schools. You must confirm your specific court has granted permission to attend traffic school before enrolling — not all violations or courts automatically qualify.

**Does California traffic school erase my ticket?**
No — California traffic school masks your ticket, it does not erase it. The conviction is held confidential from insurers and the public, but it remains on your internal DMV record. You still pay the full court fine before enrolling.

**How long is California traffic school?**
California requires a minimum of 8 hours of instruction. Most online courses are self-paced and can be completed in a single sitting or spread across multiple sessions.

---

## Colorado

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/colorado

Colorado does not have a statewide traffic-school program for points reduction or ticket dismissal — both decisions are left entirely to the individual court that issued the citation, with practices varying significantly between counties and municipalities. The mechanism most Colorado drivers use is avoiding points rather than removing them: when a court accepts a defensive-driving completion certificate, the agreement typically prevents points from being added to the Colorado DMV record in the first place rather than removing existing points. Always contact the issuing court before enrolling in any course — what works in Denver County may not be available in Boulder or El Paso. Colorado uses a points system tracked by the Department of Revenue's DMV; adult drivers face license suspension at 12 points in 12 months or 18 points in 24 months, with stricter thresholds for drivers under 21.

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Who submits my certificate in Colorado?**
The court will provide submission instructions when approving your participation. Typically the driver submits the certificate to the court by the deadline provided.

**Does Colorado defensive driving dismiss my ticket?**
Colorado has no statewide ticket dismissal program — it is entirely at individual court discretion. If approved by your court, completing a defensive driving course can dismiss your ticket, avoid points, or remove existing points. Contact your court first to determine eligibility.

**How often can I use Colorado defensive driving for ticket dismissal?**
No statewide standard — determined by the individual court handling your case.

**How long is a Colorado defensive driving course?**
Course length is determined by the individual court. The court will provide specific requirements if you are approved for ticket dismissal. Voluntary courses have timelines set by the provider.

**Can I do Colorado defensive driving online?**
Yes — both online and classroom options are available. The court determines whether an online course is acceptable for your case. Confirm with your court before enrolling online.

**Can I do Colorado traffic school online?**
Yes. Online Colorado traffic school courses are accepted by courts that allow ticket dismissal. Confirm with your specific court before enrolling.

**How often can I do Colorado traffic school?**
Ticket dismissal via traffic school is generally available once every 18 months in Colorado. Individual courts may set their own rules.

**Does Colorado traffic school dismiss my ticket?**
Colorado has no statewide ticket dismissal program. Dismissal is court-by-court. With court permission you may be able to dismiss your ticket or prevent points from being added. Colorado does NOT offer a statewide point reduction option via traffic school.

**How long is Colorado traffic school?**
Colorado defensive driving courses are 8 hours for the standard driver improvement program. Some shorter court-accepted courses take 4–6 hours.

## Connecticut

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/connecticut

Connecticut does not run a statewide online traffic-school program that dismisses a ticket or removes points. What state law does provide is an insurance benefit: under Conn. Gen. Stat. § 38a-683, drivers age 60 and older who complete an approved accident-prevention course qualify for a mandated discount on their auto-insurance premium. Younger drivers may still find an insurer that offers a voluntary discount, but that is up to the insurer. For a specific ticket, the decision rests with the court on your citation. Last checked August 2026.

**Source:** Conn. Gen. Stat. § 38a-683

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Does an online traffic course dismiss a ticket in Connecticut?**
No. Connecticut has no statewide online traffic-school program that dismisses a ticket or removes points. Whether a course helps with a specific ticket is up to the court on your citation.

**What does a defensive driving course get me in Connecticut?**
Its main statutory benefit is an insurance discount: under Conn. Gen. Stat. § 38a-683, drivers age 60 and older who complete an approved accident-prevention course qualify for a mandated auto-insurance premium discount. Younger drivers may find a voluntary discount, but that is up to the insurer.

**Does Connecticut have a driver-point system?**
Connecticut uses a point-style system for license suspension, but no approved course removes points from your record. For a specific ticket, ask the clerk of the court printed on your citation.

## Delaware

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/delaware

Delaware does not dismiss tickets through traffic school, but it does offer a voluntary benefit: completing an approved defensive driving course credits three points off your driving record and earns a 10 percent auto-insurance discount for three years (2 DE Admin Code 2224). The full course runs six hours, with a shorter three-hour refresher available. This reduces points and lowers insurance rather than dismissing the ticket, so the conviction stands. Last checked August 2026.

**Source:** 2 DE Admin Code 2224; Delaware DMV Defensive Driving Course

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Estimated all-in cost of a first speeding ticket:** $4,582 (fine plus a three-year insurance surcharge; 2026 study at https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket)

**Does traffic school dismiss a ticket in Delaware?**
No. Delaware's benefit is voluntary: completing an approved defensive driving course credits three points off your record and earns a 10 percent auto-insurance discount for three years (2 DE Admin Code 2224). The conviction still stands.

**How much does the Delaware course lower my insurance?**
State rule ties it to a 10 percent auto-insurance discount for three years (2 DE Admin Code 2224). Confirm the discount with your insurer.

**How long is the Delaware defensive driving course?**
Six hours for the full course, with a shorter three-hour refresher available (2 DE Admin Code 2224).

## Florida

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/florida

Florida drivers who receive a non-criminal moving violation can complete a 4-hour Basic Driver Improvement (BDI) course to keep points off their driving record under Fla. Stat. § 318.14(9). Election must be made within 30 days of the citation, and a driver may use this option once per 12 months and up to eight times in a lifetime (§ 318.14(9), as amended by ch. 2025-77; FLHSMV's FAQ still shows the old five-election limit). Completing BDI means adjudication is withheld: no points are added and your insurer is not notified of that violation, though the citation itself stays on your record as a withheld adjudication. BDI is not available to CDL holders or for a crash involving injuries. Florida also runs an 8-hour Intermediate Driver Improvement (IDI) course for certain repeat situations and a 12-hour Advanced Driver Improvement (ADI) course for suspension or habitual-offender cases; neither is a voluntary BDI substitute. Last checked August 2026.

**Source:** Fla. Stat. § 318.14(9); FLHSMV Basic Driver Improvement course standard

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Estimated all-in cost of a first speeding ticket:** $4,170 (fine plus a three-year insurance surcharge; 2026 study at https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket)

**Who submits my certificate to the Florida court?**
Your school submits the certificate electronically to the Florida DHSMV within 5 days of completion, and to the court shortly after. You do not need to mail anything yourself, but check with your school to confirm they handle electronic submission.

**Does Florida traffic school dismiss my ticket?**
Florida withholds adjudication rather than dismissing the ticket outright. Completing BDI means no points are added and your insurer is not notified of the violation, but the citation itself stays on your record as a withheld adjudication.

**Can I do Florida traffic school online?**
Yes. DHSMV-approved online BDI courses are accepted by all Florida courts. You must elect traffic school within 30 days of the citation date, and do not pay the ticket before electing, or you may waive your right to attend.

**How long is Florida traffic school?**
The Basic Driver Improvement (BDI) course for minor violations is 4 hours. Florida also runs an 8-hour Intermediate Driver Improvement (IDI) course for certain repeat situations and a 12-hour Advanced Driver Improvement (ADI) course for suspension or habitual-offender cases.

**How often can I elect Florida BDI?**
Once per 12 months, and up to eight times in your lifetime (s. 318.14(9), as amended in 2025). FLHSMV's FAQ still lists the old five-election limit, but the amended statute sets eight.

---

## Georgia

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/georgia

Georgia drivers can request that the Department of Driver Services (DDS) reduce up to 7 points from their license once every 5 years under O.C.G.A §40-5-86 by completing a DDS-certified Driver Improvement (defensive driving) course. Important caveat: for the 7-point reduction, the course must be 6 hours of classroom instruction — DDS does not accept online courses for points reduction (online courses can still be used for ticket dismissal at a court's discretion or for an insurance discount). The state-regulated price for a court-purposes or points-reduction course is $95. Georgia's point system runs from 2 to 6 points per violation, with a 15-point/24-month threshold triggering a license suspension for adults 21 and older, and stricter thresholds for drivers under 18.

**Source:** Georgia DDS Driver Improvement / Defensive Driving 6-hour course (dds.georgia.gov)

**Last verified:** August 2026

**How often can I do Georgia defensive driving?**
You can take a Georgia defensive driving course at any time, but the point reduction benefit is only available once every 5 years. Subsequent courses within that 5-year window do not remove additional points.

**How long is Georgia defensive driving?**
The approved course is 6 hours.

**Can I do Georgia defensive driving online?**
Yes. Georgia DDS-approved online defensive driving courses are accepted statewide.

**Who submits my certificate in Georgia?**
You submit your certificate of completion to the Georgia DDS. Once processed, the point reduction is automatically applied to your driving record.

**Does Georgia defensive driving dismiss my ticket?**
No. Georgia's approved course reduces your active points by up to 7 points and may qualify you for an insurance discount, but it does not dismiss the ticket or remove the conviction from your record. Georgia has no masking mechanism.

---

## Hawaii

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/hawaii

Hawaii's approach to defensive driving is heavily court-driven. There is no statewide dismissal program. Individual judges have discretion to accept course completion in lieu of the underlying penalty, but this varies widely across islands and jurisdictions. Confirm with your specific court before enrolling. An unapproved course completion doesn't help you if the judge won't accept it.

Approved online courses in Hawaii run about 8 hours and average $35, higher than most states due to the limited pool of approved providers. Not available for DUI or serious offenses. Individual carriers may offer voluntary discounts for course completion; Hawaii has no state-mandated discount. Where court dismissal is granted, the return on a course fee is substantial given Hawaii's above-average insurance surcharges after a ticket.

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Estimated all-in cost of a first speeding ticket:** $5,227 (fine plus a three-year insurance surcharge; 2026 study at https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket)

**Can I take defensive driving online in Hawaii?**
Sometimes. Hawaii has no statewide dismissal program. Individual judges have discretion to accept online course completion, and this varies widely across islands and jurisdictions. Confirm with your specific court before enrolling.

**How long is Hawaii defensive driving?**
Approved online courses run about 8 hours, the same as most mainland states.

**How much does Hawaii defensive driving cost?**
Course tuition averages around $35, higher than most states due to the limited pool of approved providers serving Hawaii.

**Does Hawaii defensive driving dismiss my ticket?**
Sometimes. Ticket dismissal via course completion is judge-driven, not automatic. Some Hawaii courts allow it for first offenses; others take a stricter view.

**Will my Hawaii insurance rate go down after the course?**
Hawaii has no state-mandated insurance discount for course completion. Individual carriers may offer voluntary discounts; check with your specific insurer before enrolling.

**Can I take Hawaii defensive driving for a DUI or reckless driving charge?**
No. Hawaii defensive driving is not available for DUI, reckless driving, or other serious offenses. It is intended for minor moving violations only.

## Idaho

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/idaho

Idaho does not dismiss tickets through traffic school. What it offers is a point reduction: completing an approved six-hour defensive driving course takes three points off your driving record (IDAPA 39.02.71). This lowers your point total rather than dismissing the ticket, so the conviction stands. Confirm your eligibility with the Idaho Transportation Department before you enroll. Last checked August 2026.

**Source:** IDAPA 39.02.71

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Does traffic school dismiss a ticket in Idaho?**
No. Idaho's benefit is a point reduction: completing an approved defensive driving course reduces three points from your record (IDAPA 39.02.71). The conviction still stands.

**How long is the Idaho defensive driving course?**
Six hours (IDAPA 39.02.71).

**How often can I reduce points in Idaho?**
The point reduction follows the schedule set by rule (IDAPA 39.02.71). Confirm your eligibility with the Idaho Transportation Department before you enroll.

## Illinois

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/illinois

Illinois drivers cited for most petty traffic offenses can avoid a conviction by pleading guilty and requesting court supervision, the dismissal mechanism authorized under 730 ILCS 5/5-6-1. Under court supervision, the judge typically requires payment of fines, court costs, and — when the court orders it — completion of a traffic safety school within a supervision period (commonly 4 months in Cook County, which uses the National Safety Council's 4-hour course). If you complete the conditions, the case is dismissed without a conviction: no points are added to your driving record and the ticket does not count toward the three-in-12-months threshold that triggers a Secretary of State suspension. Eligibility is limited to twice within any 12-month period, and supervision is unavailable for CDL holders, school-zone speeding, and second-offense driving without insurance. Last checked August 2026.

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Can I do Illinois traffic school online to fix a ticket?**
Not as a retail course you buy yourself. Illinois keeps a ticket off your record through court supervision, not an online defensive-driving product. If the court orders traffic safety school as a supervision condition, the format is set by your county — Cook County, for example, uses the National Safety Council's course in a classroom or online. Ask the court on your citation what it requires.

**Does Illinois traffic school reduce points on my license?**
No. Illinois has an administrative point system (92 Ill. Adm. Code 1040.20), but no course reduces points. Points matter only toward a suspension after three moving-violation convictions in 12 months (625 ILCS 5/6-206). The way to avoid a conviction is court supervision, not a point-reduction course.

**How does court supervision work in Illinois?**
You plead guilty and ask the judge for court supervision (730 ILCS 5/5-6-1). The judge defers judgment and sets conditions — typically fines and court costs, and sometimes traffic safety school. Complete them within the supervision period and the case is dismissed without a conviction (730 ILCS 5/5-6-3.1), so no points are added and it does not count toward the three-in-12-months suspension threshold.

**How often can I get court supervision in Illinois?**
Court supervision is limited to twice within any 12-month period (730 ILCS 5/5-6-1(k)). It is generally unavailable to CDL holders, for school-zone speeding, and for a second offense of driving without insurance.

**Does a course dismiss my Illinois ticket by itself?**
No. Only the court can dismiss the ticket, through supervision. A traffic safety course is one possible condition of supervision, ordered at the court's discretion — it is not a standalone dismissal you can buy online. Confirm the details with the court on your citation.

## Indiana

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/indiana

Indiana does not dismiss tickets through traffic school. Its benefit is a point credit: completing an approved four-hour BMV Driver Safety Program course takes four points off your driving record (IC 9-30-3-12). This reduces your point total rather than dismissing the ticket, so the conviction stands. Last checked August 2026.

**Source:** IC 9-30-3-12; Indiana BMV Driver Safety Program

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Does traffic school dismiss a ticket in Indiana?**
No. Indiana's benefit is a point credit: completing an approved four-hour BMV Driver Safety Program course credits four points off your record (IC 9-30-3-12). The conviction still stands.

**How long is the Indiana Driver Safety Program course?**
Four hours (IC 9-30-3-12; Indiana BMV Driver Safety Program).

**How many points does the Indiana course credit?**
Four points, credited off your driving record on the schedule set by the BMV (IC 9-30-3-12).

## Iowa

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/iowa

Iowa courts have discretion to accept an Iowa DOT-approved defensive driving course as an alternative to accumulating points on your driving record. The mechanism is judge-driven, not automatic. Not every Iowa court accepts it, so verify with the specific court handling your case before enrolling.

Iowa DOT-approved online courses run about 6 hours and typically cost $20. Where the court accepts course completion, the ticket is prevented from generating an insurance surcharge. Individual carriers may offer voluntary discounts for course completion, though there is no state-mandated discount. Not available for DUI or commercial vehicle violations. Ask about court acceptance at your court appearance before spending on a course.

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Can I take defensive driving online in Iowa?**
Yes. Iowa DOT-approved online defensive driving courses are accepted by many Iowa courts as an alternative to accumulating points. Court approval varies by jurisdiction, so confirm with your specific court before enrolling.

**How long is Iowa defensive driving?**
Approved online courses run about 6 hours.

**How much does Iowa defensive driving cost?**
Course tuition typically runs $19.95 to $25 for Iowa DOT-approved online providers.

**Does Iowa defensive driving dismiss my ticket?**
At court discretion. Some Iowa judges accept course completion in lieu of points or as part of a reduced charge. Ask about court acceptance at your court appearance before spending on a course.

**Will my Iowa insurance rate go down after the course?**
Some Iowa carriers offer voluntary discounts for approved course completion. There is no state-mandated discount. Check with your specific insurer before enrolling.

**Can I take Iowa defensive driving for a DUI or reckless driving charge?**
No. Iowa defensive driving is not available for DUI, reckless driving, or commercial vehicle violations.

## Kansas

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/kansas

Kansas does not use a driver point system — the Department of Revenue's Division of Vehicles tracks violations by count rather than numeric points, and three moving-violation convictions within any 12-month period can trigger a license suspension (K.S.A. 8-255). Whether traffic school can dismiss a ticket is decided court by court at the county or municipal level, typically through a diversion agreement with the prosecutor (K.S.A. 22-2906) that requires payment of court fees, completion of an approved defensive driving course, and a clean record for a set probation period. Eligibility, and whether a course is accepted at all, is set by that court, so there is no statewide course length. Kansas does separately mandate an auto-insurance discount: completing an approved course of at least four hours entitles eligible drivers to a three-year premium reduction, with the amount set by each insurer (K.S.A. 40-1112a). Always contact the issuing court before enrolling — what's available in Sedgwick County may differ from Johnson County or Shawnee County. Last checked August 2026.

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Does Kansas traffic school dismiss my ticket?**
Not on its own. Kansas has no statewide dismissal program and no driver point system. Dismissal is handled court by court through a prosecutorial diversion agreement (K.S.A. 22-2906); where a court accepts it, completing an approved course can be part of that agreement. Eligibility depends on your court, your violation, and your record, so check with the court on your citation before enrolling.

**Can I do Kansas defensive driving online?**
Yes. Kansas defensive driving courses are available fully online. Whether a court accepts one toward a diversion is up to that court, but an approved online course does count toward the state's mandatory insurance discount.

**Does Kansas give an insurance discount for defensive driving?**
Yes. Kansas law requires insurers to give a three-year premium reduction to a driver who completes an approved course of at least four hours (K.S.A. 40-1112a). The discount amount is set by each insurer. This is separate from anything to do with your ticket.

**How long is a Kansas defensive driving course?**
There is no statewide length for ticket dismissal — each court's diversion agreement sets its own requirement. For the mandatory insurance discount, the course must be at least four hours (K.S.A. 40-1112a).

**Who submits my certificate in Kansas?**
You do. Your provider sends you the completion certificate, and you submit it to the court (for a diversion) or to your insurer (for the discount). The exact method is set by your court.

---

## Kentucky

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/kentucky

Kentucky's State Traffic School can prevent points from being added to your driving record, but only when the court refers you to it as part of your case (KRS 186.574). The referral is not automatic and there is no voluntary sign-up: you have to request it at your court appearance, and the judge decides. Completion withholds the points, yet the conviction itself still stands — it is not a dismissal. The only Transportation Cabinet-approved online version is the state's contractor, RightLane, which runs about 4 hours ($39 online, or $15 in a classroom); a national online course does not satisfy a Kentucky referral, and the course must be finished within 30 days. Completion is generally allowed once every 12 months. Ask your court clerk about State Traffic School eligibility before you enter a plea. Last checked August 2026.

**Source:** 601 KAR 13:025; drive.ky.gov Kentucky State Traffic School

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Can I take Kentucky State Traffic School online?**
Yes, but only when the court refers you, and only through the Transportation Cabinet's contractor, RightLane. It runs about 4 hours ($39 online, $15 in a classroom) and must be finished within 30 days of referral. A national online course you buy on your own does not satisfy a Kentucky referral (KRS 186.574).

**Does Kentucky State Traffic School dismiss my ticket?**
No. Completion keeps points from being added to your record, but the conviction still stands — it is not a dismissal. Actual dismissal, where it is offered, comes from a separate county-attorney diversion (KRS 186.574(6)), decided case by case. Ask the court on your citation which options apply.

**Can I just sign up for a Kentucky course myself?**
No. Kentucky State Traffic School is court-referral only — there is no voluntary enrollment. You have to request it at your court appearance and the judge decides (601 KAR 13:025).

**How much does it cost and how often can I take it?**
RightLane, the state's approved online provider, charges $39 online ($15 for the classroom version). Completion is generally allowed once every 12 months, measured from your most recent completion date.

**Will my Kentucky insurance go down after the course?**
Maybe. Some Kentucky carriers offer a voluntary discount for approved course completion, but it is not state-mandated. Check with your own insurer before enrolling.

---

## Louisiana

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/louisiana

Louisiana does not use a driver point system — the Office of Motor Vehicles (OMV) tracks the type and frequency of traffic violations on the Official Driving Record instead. Whether traffic school can dismiss a misdemeanor Title 32 moving violation (speeding under 25 mph over the limit, running a stop sign, driving under suspension, etc.) is decided court-by-court at the parish level; many parishes accept state-approved online courses with prior court permission, while others do not. Title 14 offenses (DWI, reckless operation, hit-and-run) cannot be dismissed through traffic school. Louisiana's insurance discount has direct statutory authority — under Louisiana Revised Statutes 22:1457, completing an approved defensive driving course entitles eligible drivers to a 10% reduction in liability and collision premiums for three consecutive years.

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Estimated all-in cost of a first speeding ticket:** $4,512 (fine plus a three-year insurance surcharge; 2026 study at https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket)

**How often can I use Louisiana defensive driving?**
A Louisiana traffic school certificate can only be used once within a two-year period to dismiss a charge from your driving record.

**Can I do Louisiana defensive driving online?**
Yes. Louisiana defensive driving courses are available fully online statewide and are accepted by most courts for ticket dismissal and by insurers for the 10% discount.

**How long is Louisiana defensive driving?**
Louisiana defensive driving courses range from 4 to 6 hours depending on the provider and court requirement. The OMV states courses may take anywhere from 4 to 12 hours; most courts require 6 hours for dismissal.

**Who submits my certificate in Louisiana?**
You receive your completion certificate from your provider (by email or print) and submit it to the court yourself. Submission method varies by court — confirm with your specific parish court.

**Does Louisiana traffic school dismiss my ticket?**
Louisiana has no statewide ticket dismissal program. Dismissal is court-by-court under Louisiana Code of Criminal Procedure Article 892.1, which allows courts to dismiss Title 32 moving violation misdemeanors. Louisiana has no point system.

**How long is Louisiana traffic school?**
Louisiana requires a minimum of 6 hours for a state-approved defensive driving course. Online and in-person formats both qualify at this length.

**Can I do Louisiana traffic school online?**
Yes. Louisiana OMV-approved online courses are available statewide. Online is the most convenient option because the school reports your completion directly to the OMV without any action required from you.

## Maine

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/maine

Maine does not currently accept online defensive driving courses for ticket dismissal, point reduction, or state-mandated insurance discount. Maine's Bureau of Motor Vehicles maintains in-person driver improvement programs, but these are typically assigned by the BMV after multiple violations rather than being voluntary.

For a Maine driver looking at a routine speeding ticket, the primary options for reducing the insurance impact are contesting the ticket at court or negotiating a reduced charge, often with the assistance of a traffic attorney familiar with the specific court. Online defensive driving, while widely marketed nationally, does not offer a legitimate benefit in Maine. Any provider claiming otherwise for Maine drivers should be viewed with skepticism.

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Estimated all-in cost of a first speeding ticket:** $2,100 (fine plus a three-year insurance surcharge; 2026 study at https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket)

**Can I take defensive driving online in Maine?**
No. Maine does not accept any online defensive driving course for ticket dismissal or points. The only course that earns a record credit is the state's classroom Driving Dynamics program; a national online course does nothing for a Maine ticket.

**Does any Maine course reduce points on my record?**
Yes, but only in a classroom. Completing the state's Driving Dynamics course earns a three-point credit on your driving record. It is a 5-hour classroom course ($70) run by the Maine Bureau of Highway Safety through local adult education programs. There is no approved online version.

**What driver improvement options does Maine offer?**
Beyond Driving Dynamics, the Maine Bureau of Motor Vehicles runs in-person driver improvement programs, but these are typically assigned by the BMV after multiple violations rather than chosen voluntarily.

**Are there Maine insurance discounts for course completion?**
There is no state-mandated insurance discount for a defensive driving course in Maine. Some individual carriers offer a voluntary discount for approved programs, but it is the exception — ask your insurer.

**Why do national providers advertise Maine defensive driving?**
National providers often list all 50 states in their marketing without noting state-level exceptions. Maine, along with Massachusetts, New Hampshire, and Vermont, does not accept online courses for standard driver relief. Verify before purchasing.

## Maryland

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/maryland

Maryland has no voluntary online course that dismisses a ticket or takes points off your record. What the state runs is the Driver Improvement Program, a remedial course the MVA or a court assigns, usually after you accumulate points or as a condition for new drivers. Completing it satisfies that requirement and helps you avoid further action, but it does not remove points or dismiss the ticket, and your points fall off only with time. Contact the MVA or the court on your citation to learn what applies to you. Last checked August 2026.

**Source:** Maryland MVA Driver Improvement Program

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Estimated all-in cost of a first speeding ticket:** $1,869 (fine plus a three-year insurance surcharge; 2026 study at https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket)

**Does an online course dismiss a ticket or remove points in Maryland?**
No. Maryland has no voluntary course that dismisses a ticket or removes points. The Driver Improvement Program is a remedial course the MVA or a court assigns; completing it satisfies that requirement rather than clearing points.

**Who has to take the Maryland Driver Improvement Program?**
Drivers the MVA assigns after points accumulate, certain new drivers, or drivers a court orders to it. It is four to eight hours (Maryland MVA).

**How do points come off my Maryland record?**
With time. No course removes them. For your ticket, contact the MVA or the court on your citation.

## Massachusetts

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/massachusetts

Massachusetts does not currently accept online defensive driving courses for ticket dismissal, point reduction, or insurance discount. The state's Driver Retraining Program is classroom-only, and it is generally only available to drivers assigned by the Registry of Motor Vehicles after multiple violations.

Massachusetts operates a Safe Driver Insurance Plan (SDIP) rather than a traditional point system. Traffic violations affect insurance surcharges directly, calculated by the Merit Rating Board. For a Massachusetts driver looking at a routine speeding ticket, the strongest paths to reducing the insurance impact are contesting the ticket at the magistrate hearing or negotiating a lesser charge with the assistance of a traffic attorney. Online defensive driving, while widely marketed nationally, is not a legitimate option here. Any provider claiming otherwise for MA drivers is worth avoiding.

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Can I take defensive driving online in Massachusetts?**
No. Massachusetts does not accept online defensive driving courses for ticket dismissal, point reduction, or insurance discount. Any provider claiming otherwise for MA drivers is not offering a legitimate course.

**Does Massachusetts have a traditional point system?**
No. Massachusetts operates under the Safe Driver Insurance Plan (SDIP), managed by the Merit Rating Board. Traffic violations affect insurance surcharges directly rather than accumulating demerit points.

**What is the Massachusetts Driver Retraining Program?**
A classroom-only program run through the Registry of Motor Vehicles. It is typically assigned to drivers after multiple violations, not something drivers can voluntarily enroll in for a discount.

**How can I reduce the insurance impact of a Massachusetts ticket?**
The primary options are contesting the ticket at the magistrate hearing or negotiating a lesser charge, often with the assistance of a traffic attorney familiar with the specific court.

**Are there any state-approved Massachusetts insurance discounts for course completion?**
No state-mandated discount for defensive driving course completion exists. Some individual carriers offer voluntary discounts for professional driving programs, but not for standard defensive driving.

## Michigan

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/michigan

Michigan drivers can avoid points and prevent insurer notification by completing a Basic Driver Improvement Course (BDIC) under MCL 257.320d, but the program is once in a lifetime and only offered when the Secretary of State sends a notice of eligibility. To qualify, you need a valid non-commercial Michigan license with 2 or fewer points already on record, and the ticket must carry 3 points or fewer and not involve careless or negligent driving. The course is at least 4 hours, capped by state law at $100, and must be completed within 60 days of the eligibility notice — there are no extensions. Passing means the ticket appears on your driving record but the points and the insurer-reportable detail are withheld; failing the course or missing the 60-day window means full point assessment.

**Source:** MCL 257.320d; Michigan SOS Basic Driver Improvement Course (invitation-only)

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Estimated all-in cost of a first speeding ticket:** $8,742 (fine plus a three-year insurance surcharge; 2026 study at https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket)

**Who submits my certificate in Michigan?**
Your course provider notifies the Michigan Secretary of State electronically, typically within 1–2 business days of completion. You will also receive a certificate by mail, but you do not need to submit it anywhere yourself — the school handles state reporting.

**Does Michigan traffic school dismiss my ticket?**
Michigan’s Basic Driver Improvement Course (BDIC) does not dismiss your ticket. Instead, it allows eligible drivers to avoid points being added to their record for the cited violation. You must receive an eligibility notice from the Michigan Secretary of State (SOS) before you can enroll — you cannot self-select into the program.

**How often can I take the Michigan BDIC?**
Eligibility is controlled by the Michigan SOS, which mails a notification when you qualify. You must complete the course within 60 days of receiving the eligibility letter. You cannot enroll without this notification.

**Can I do Michigan BDIC online?**
Yes. Michigan Secretary of State-approved online BDIC courses are available.

**How long is the Michigan BDIC?**
The Michigan BDIC is a minimum of 4 hours. Courses cannot legally charge more than $100.

**Can I do Michigan driver improvement online?**
Yes. Michigan SOS-approved BDIC courses are available fully online, accessible 24/7 from any internet-connected device.

**How long is Michigan driver improvement?**
The Michigan BDIC is a minimum of 4 hours. All SOS-approved providers use the same 4-hour minimum.

**How often can I do Michigan driver improvement?**
Michigan's BDIC benefit is available only ONCE IN A LIFETIME — not on a periodic cooldown cycle. Once you have used it, you cannot use it again for any future ticket.

**How long is Michigan traffic school?**
Michigan's Driver Improvement Program requires 8 hours of instruction. This applies to all approved formats, including online courses.

**Can I do Michigan traffic school online?**
Yes. Online driver improvement courses are fully approved in Michigan. You can complete the course from home through a state-approved provider.

## Minnesota

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/minnesota

Minnesota has no driver-point system, and no statewide traffic-school program dismisses a ticket here. What state law does provide is an insurance benefit: under Minn. Stat. § 65B.28, drivers age 55 and older who complete an approved accident-prevention course qualify for an auto-insurance premium reduction of at least 10 percent for three years. Younger drivers may still find an insurer offering a voluntary discount, but that is the insurer's call. For a specific ticket, the decision rests with the court on your citation. Last checked August 2026.

**Source:** Minn. Stat. § 65B.28

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Does an online traffic course dismiss a ticket in Minnesota?**
No. Minnesota has no driver-point system and no statewide traffic-school program that dismisses a ticket. Any handling of a specific ticket is up to the court on your citation.

**What does a defensive driving course get me in Minnesota?**
Its main statutory benefit is an insurance reduction: under Minn. Stat. § 65B.28, drivers age 55 and older who complete an approved accident-prevention course qualify for an auto-insurance premium reduction of at least 10 percent for three years.

**Does Minnesota have a driver-point system?**
No. Minnesota does not assign points to your license, so there are no points for a course to remove. For a specific ticket, ask the clerk of the court printed on your citation.

## Mississippi

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/mississippi

Mississippi lets you keep a conviction off your record through nonadjudication: with the court's agreement, completing an approved course means the ticket is not entered as a conviction. It is available once every three years for an eligible moving violation (Miss. Code § 63-9-11). Because it runs through the court, confirm eligibility with the court on your citation before you enroll. Last checked August 2026.

**Source:** Miss. Code § 63-9-11

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Can traffic school keep a ticket off my record in Mississippi?**
Yes, through nonadjudication. With the court's agreement, completing an approved course means the ticket is not entered as a conviction (Miss. Code § 63-9-11).

**How often can I use nonadjudication in Mississippi?**
Once every three years, not once per lifetime (Miss. Code § 63-9-11). Confirm eligibility with the court on your citation.

**How long is the Mississippi course?**
Four hours (Miss. Code § 63-9-11).

## Missouri

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/missouri

Missouri does not dismiss tickets through traffic school, but it does allow a point reduction. With the court's approval, completing an approved eight-hour Driver Improvement Program course reduces points on your record (RSMo § 302.302). You must finish within 60 days of the violation, it is available once in any 36-month period, and commercial-license holders are not eligible. Because it needs court approval, ask the court printed on your citation before you enroll. Last checked August 2026.

**Source:** RSMo § 302.302

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Does traffic school dismiss a ticket in Missouri?**
No. With the court's approval, an approved eight-hour Driver Improvement Program course reduces points on your record (RSMo § 302.302). The conviction still stands.

**How often can I use the Missouri point reduction?**
Once in any 36-month period, and you must complete the course within 60 days of the violation (RSMo § 302.302). Commercial-license holders are not eligible.

**How long is the Missouri course?**
Eight hours, meeting the National Safety Council standard (RSMo § 302.302).

## Montana

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/montana

Montana operates a Driver Rehabilitation Point System under ARM 23.3.202, administered by the Motor Vehicle Division (MVD) of the Department of Justice. Points stay on the driving record for 3 years from conviction date, and accumulating 30 conviction points within 3 years results in being declared a Habitual Traffic Offender, which can lead to a 3-year license revocation. Unlike many states, Montana does not have a statewide voluntary point-reduction program through traffic school — completing an approved defensive driving course will not directly remove existing points from the record. Whether traffic school can dismiss a ticket is decided court-by-court at the city, justice, or municipal court level, typically with conditions like a clean driving history and a violation under 25 mph over the limit. Drivers whose licenses have been suspended can complete a defensive driving course to reduce their reinstatement fee by up to 50%. Montana law mandates an auto insurance discount for drivers 55 and older who complete an approved defensive driving course; younger drivers may receive a discount at their insurer's discretion.

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Estimated all-in cost of a first speeding ticket:** $1,486 (fine plus a three-year insurance surcharge; 2026 study at https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket)

**Does Montana have a driver license point system?**
Yes. Montana uses a Driver Rehabilitation Point System under Administrative Rules of Montana 23.3.202, administered by the Motor Vehicle Division (MVD) of the Department of Justice. Points are assigned for moving-violation convictions and stay on the record for 3 years from conviction date. Accumulating 30 conviction points within a 3-year period results in being declared a Habitual Traffic Offender, which can lead to a 3-year license revocation.

**Can I take a defensive driving course to remove points from my Montana driving record?**
No. Montana does not offer a statewide voluntary point-reduction program — completing a defensive driving course does not directly remove points from the MVD record. Points are removed automatically 3 years after the conviction date. The only path drivers have to reduce their record is waiting out that 3-year window.

**Can I take traffic school to dismiss a Montana traffic ticket?**
Possibly, but only with court permission. Montana has no statewide ticket-dismissal program, so each city, justice, or municipal court decides on a case-by-case basis whether to allow defensive driving as a path to dismissal. Most courts that do allow it require a clean recent driving record and limit eligibility to minor moving violations (typically not speeding 25+ mph over the limit, accidents, or reckless driving). Contact the court that issued the ticket before enrolling.

**Does Montana require auto insurers to give a discount for completing a defensive driving course?**
Yes, but only for drivers 55 and older. Montana law mandates that auto insurance carriers offer a premium discount to drivers age 55+ who complete an approved defensive driving course. Drivers under 55 may still be offered a discount at the insurer's discretion — contact your carrier to confirm eligibility before enrolling.

**What happens if my Montana driver's license is suspended for points?**
Drivers who are suspended, or who have served at least one year of a 3-year revocation, can participate in Montana's driver rehabilitation program. Participants may be required to complete driver-safety courses and retake the licensing exam, and qualified participants are eligible for a restricted license usable for travel to and from work or school during the suspension or revocation period. Completing a defensive driving course can also reduce the license reinstatement fee by up to 50%.

**Does Montana online traffic school count for ticket dismissal?**
Whether an online course qualifies depends entirely on the court that issued the ticket. Some Montana courts accept MVD-recognized online providers; others require classroom-based courses or do not allow defensive driving for dismissal at all. The course must be completed before the deadline the court sets (commonly 30–90 days), and the certificate must be filed with the court. Always confirm acceptance and format with the court before paying for an online course.

## Nebraska

Nebraska drivers can complete an approved driver-improvement course to credit two points off their driving record. Under Neb. Rev. Stat. § 60-4,188 the course runs at least four hours and the two-point credit is available once within any five-year period. This reduces points rather than dismissing the ticket, so the conviction stands. Ticket dismissal, where a county offers it, runs through a separate court diversion. Last checked August 2026.

The conviction still stands. Ticket dismissal, where a county offers it, runs through a separate court diversion.

**How long is the Nebraska driver-improvement course?**
At least four hours of instruction, under Neb. Rev. Stat. § 60-4,188.

Once within any five-year period (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 60-4,188). Confirm your eligibility with the Nebraska DMV before you enroll.

## Nevada

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/nevada

Nevada does not dismiss tickets through traffic school. Its benefit is a point removal: completing a DMV-approved traffic safety school course takes three demerit points off your record (Nevada DMV; NAC 483.787). The standard course runs five hours, or eight hours if you have three or more violations. Note that a course taken as part of a plea bargain earns no point credit. This reduces points rather than dismissing the ticket, so the conviction stands. Last checked August 2026.

**Source:** Nevada DMV Traffic Safety Schools; NAC 483.787

**Last verified:** August 2026

No. A DMV-approved traffic safety school course removes three demerit points from your record (NAC 483.787). The conviction still stands.

**How long is the Nevada traffic safety course?**
Five hours for the standard course, or eight hours for drivers with three or more violations (Nevada DMV; NAC 483.787).

**Does a plea-bargain course remove points in Nevada?**
No. A course taken as part of a plea bargain does not earn the point credit (Nevada DMV). The point removal is for a voluntary DMV-approved course.

## New Jersey

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/new-jersey

New Jersey's MVC-approved Defensive Driving Course provides two mandated benefits for eligible drivers: a 2-point reduction on the driving record, and an insurance discount of 5% to 10% for three years on liability, personal injury protection, and collision coverage (NJ Admin Code 11:3-24.4). The course does not dismiss the underlying ticket. The conviction still appears on the record.

Approved online courses run about 6 hours. Course tuition averages $25. The point reduction is available once every five years, the insurance discount once every three years. The mandated discount is worth several hundred dollars per year on the average New Jersey premium, one of the strongest structured discount programs in the country. New Jersey drivers with any moving violation on their record should consider the course as a routine hedge, not an emergency response.

**Source:** N.J.A.C. 13:21-24.5 (minimum 6 hours of instruction); NJ MVC-approved Defensive Driving Course

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Estimated all-in cost of a first speeding ticket:** $4,965 (fine plus a three-year insurance surcharge; 2026 study at https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket)

**Can I take defensive driving online in New Jersey?**
Yes. New Jersey MVC-approved online Defensive Driving Courses provide a 2-point reduction on your driving record and qualify you for a mandated insurance discount.

**How much is the New Jersey insurance discount?**
New Jersey law mandates a 5% to 10% discount on liability, personal injury protection, and collision coverage for 3 years after approved course completion (NJ Admin Code 11:3-24.4).

**How long is the New Jersey Defensive Driving Course?**
Approved online courses run about 6 hours. Drivers can complete the material across multiple sittings.

**How much does the New Jersey course cost?**
Course tuition typically runs $25 to $50 for MVC-approved online providers.

**Does the course dismiss my New Jersey ticket?**
No. The ticket stays on your record. The course reduces 2 points and triggers the mandated insurance discount. Ticket dismissal in New Jersey is not available through online defensive driving.

**How often can I take the New Jersey course?**
The 2-point reduction is available once every five years. The insurance discount is available once every three years.

**What is the difference between the Defensive Driving Course and the Driver Improvement Program?**
The MVC-approved online Defensive Driving Course is voluntary and gives a 2-point reduction plus insurance discount. The Driver Improvement Program (DIP) is classroom-only, MVC-initiated for drivers with 12-14 points, and removes up to 3 points.

## New Mexico

Ask the specific court about dismissal-via-course before entering a plea. New Mexico's rural highway network makes speeding tickets common, and the state's defensive driving option is genuinely useful for drivers who act before pleading.

## New York

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/new-york

New York drivers can complete a DMV-approved Point and Insurance Reduction Program (PIRP), also known as the Defensive Driving Course or Accident Prevention Course, to remove up to 4 active points from their record and earn a mandatory 10% auto liability and collision insurance discount for 3 years under NY Insurance Law § 2336. The course is a minimum of 320 minutes (5 hours, 20 minutes) of instruction, whether taken online or in-person, and is available to drivers of all license classes. Point reduction applies only to points accumulated within the 18 months before course completion and is allowed once every 18 months. PIRP does not dismiss tickets and the violation conviction stays on the driving record; it offsets points for the DMV's 11-point/18-month suspension threshold and the Driver Responsibility Assessment fee thresholds. Last checked August 2026.

**Source:** NY DMV Point & Insurance Reduction Program, 320-minute minimum (dmv.ny.gov)

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Estimated all-in cost of a first speeding ticket:** $2,553 (fine plus a three-year insurance surcharge; 2026 study at https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket)

**How long is New York PIRP?**
The course is 320 minutes (5 hours, 20 minutes), the state minimum, whether online or in a classroom. Providers often schedule it as a 6-hour session that includes breaks.

**How often can I take New York PIRP?**
Once every 18 months for the point-reduction benefit. You can retake it every 3 years to renew your 10% insurance discount. Only violations from the 18 months before course completion are eligible for the point reduction.

**Does New York defensive driving dismiss my ticket?**
No. New York's Point and Insurance Reduction Program (PIRP) does not dismiss tickets or remove violations from your driving record. It reduces your active point total by up to 4 points and earns a mandatory 10% auto insurance discount for 3 years — but the underlying ticket remains.

**Who submits my PIRP certificate in New York?**
Your school reports completion electronically to the NY DMV, which automatically applies the point reduction. You submit the certificate to your insurance company yourself to receive the 10% discount.

**Can I do New York PIRP online?**
Yes. NY DMV-approved online PIRP courses are accepted statewide. The course is not court-ordered — any licensed NY driver can take it voluntarily to earn point reduction and insurance benefits.

**How long is New York traffic school?**
New York's PIRP is 320 minutes (5 hours, 20 minutes) of instruction. This applies to all approved formats, including fully online courses; providers may schedule a longer session to include breaks.

**How often can I do New York traffic school?**
You can take New York's PIRP once every 18 months for point reduction. The 18-month period runs from the completion date of your most recent PIRP course.

**Does New York traffic school dismiss my ticket?**
No. New York's PIRP does not dismiss your ticket — the conviction still appears on your driving record. It reduces up to 4 points from your DMV abstract and qualifies you for a 10% insurance discount for 3 years. Think of it as damage control rather than erasure.

**Can I do New York traffic school online?**
Yes. New York's PIRP is available fully online through DMV-approved providers. You can complete the course at your own pace from any device.

## North Carolina

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/north-carolina

North Carolina's Prayer for Judgment Continued (PJC) is a common-law remedy unique to the state — a defendant pleads guilty to a traffic offense, and the judge, at their discretion, "continues" entering a final judgment. No points are assessed against the license, no fine is imposed (though court costs of roughly $190–$210 still apply), and the violation is not reported as a conviction for insurance or DMV purposes. PJCs are limited: insurance carriers count only one PJC per household every 3 years for premium-rate purposes, and the NC DMV recognizes only two PJCs per driver every 5 years. PJCs are not available for speeding 25+ mph over the limit, DWI, passing a stopped school bus, or any offense by a CDL holder. Online defensive-driving courses in NC are an insurance-discount tool only — they do not affect points or the underlying conviction.

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Estimated all-in cost of a first speeding ticket:** $3,938 (fine plus a three-year insurance surcharge; 2026 study at https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket)

**Does traffic school dismiss a ticket in North Carolina?**
Not on its own. Dismissal requires prior court permission on a per-case basis, and eligibility depends on the violation, your driving history, and prosecutor policy. Many drivers instead use a Prayer for Judgment Continued (PJC), a separate step where the judge delays entering judgment; for insurance purposes it is limited to once every three years per household.

**How do I reduce points in North Carolina?**
Point reduction through defensive driving requires 7 or more DMV license points on your record plus a $40 DMV eligibility hearing, and it is available only once every five years.

**How long is the North Carolina course?**
It depends on the county: Wake and Guilford counties require a 4-hour course; all other North Carolina counties require 8 hours.

## North Dakota

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/north-dakota

North Dakota drivers can use an NDDOT-approved online defensive driving course for point reduction on their driving record. Ticket dismissal is possible with court approval, but this varies by jurisdiction and isn't automatic.

Approved online courses in North Dakota run about 6 hours and typically cost $20 to $25. The course reduces points on the driving record, which manages license risk and can affect carrier renewal scoring. Individual insurers may offer voluntary discounts for course completion, though there is no state-mandated discount. Course completion is generally allowed once every 12 months. Where court dismissal is granted, the return on a course fee is meaningful given North Dakota's average insurance surcharge patterns.

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Can I take defensive driving online in North Dakota?**
Yes. NDDOT-approved online defensive driving courses are accepted statewide for point reduction. Court-driven ticket dismissal is also available in many jurisdictions.

**How long is North Dakota defensive driving?**
Approved online courses run about 6 hours.

**How much does North Dakota defensive driving cost?**
Course tuition typically runs $19.95 to $25 for NDDOT-approved online providers.

**Does North Dakota defensive driving dismiss my ticket?**
With court approval, yes. The mechanism is court-driven, not automatic. Confirm with your specific court before enrolling.

**How often can I take North Dakota defensive driving?**
Once per 12 months. The 12-month clock starts from your most recent completion date.

**Will my North Dakota insurance go down after the course?**
Some North Dakota carriers offer voluntary discounts for approved course completion. There is no state-mandated discount. Check with your specific insurer before enrolling.

## Ohio

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/ohio

Ohio drivers with 2 to 11 points on their license can complete an 8-hour Adult Remedial Driving Course (sometimes called Defensive Driving) to receive a 2-point credit on their driving record under Ohio Revised Code §4510.037(C). The credit is a buffer rather than a true point removal — the conviction remains on the record, and the credit only offsets points already assessed; it does not dismiss tickets. The option is available once every 3 years and the course must be completed at a state-approved provider. Drivers who accumulate 12 points within any 2-year window face a mandatory 6-month license suspension; the BMV mails a warning letter at 6 points, and the 2-point credit is most useful for drivers in the 6–11 point range trying to avoid that threshold.

**Source:** Ohio Adm. Code 4501-21-06 (remedial/driver-safety course)

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Estimated all-in cost of a first speeding ticket:** $1,684 (fine plus a three-year insurance surcharge; 2026 study at https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket)

**Does traffic school dismiss a ticket in Ohio?**
Not automatically. Ohio courts may allow a dismissal or a reduced fine when you complete an approved defensive driving course, but that is at the court's discretion. Confirm with the court on your citation before you enroll.

**Can a course reduce points on my Ohio record?**
Yes. Completing a Bureau of Motor Vehicles-approved remedial driver-safety course can reduce points on your driving record. Confirm your current eligibility with the Ohio BMV.

**How long is the Ohio course?**
Eight hours (Ohio Adm. Code 4501-21-06).

## Oklahoma

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/oklahoma

Oklahoma drivers can remove 2 points from their driving record by completing a state-approved 6-hour Driver Improvement / Defensive Driving Course under 47 O.S. §6-206.1, available once every 24 months. To qualify under the statute, drivers must hold a valid Oklahoma driver's license and have no more than 5 points accumulated in the prior 3 years. Service Oklahoma (formerly DPS) tracks points through the Mandatory Point System; 10 or more points within 5 years triggers a license suspension. As of August 2025, federal law (Title 49 §384.226) prohibits the 2-point reduction for CDL holders, even on personal vehicle violations. Standard Motor Vehicle Accident Prevention Courses do not qualify for the 2-point credit — only courses specifically approved as Driver Improvement / Defensive Driving programs by Service Oklahoma do.

**Source:** 47 O.S. § 6-206.1; Service Oklahoma defensive driving course

**Last verified:** August 2026

**How long is Oklahoma defensive driving?**
Oklahoma DPS-approved defensive driving courses are 6 hours. This applies to all DPS-approved providers.

**How often can I do Oklahoma defensive driving?**
The 2-point DPS reduction can be applied once every 24 months. For court-ordered ticket dismissal, the court sets its own rules.

**Does Oklahoma traffic school dismiss my ticket?**
Yes. With court approval, completing an Oklahoma defensive driving course can dismiss a moving violation from your record. The course also provides a 2-point reduction on your DPS record.

**Who submits my certificate in Oklahoma?**
For Oklahoma City Court, Cleveland Municipal, and Jones Municipal: provider sends certificate to court within 24 hours. For all other courts: certificate is mailed to driver, who must then submit it to the court.

**Can I do Oklahoma defensive driving online?**
Yes. Online courses are accepted by Oklahoma courts for ticket dismissal. Note: online courses do not qualify for the DPS 2-point reduction — only in-person classroom courses qualify for that benefit.

## Oregon

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/oregon

Oregon does not use a traditional demerit points system. Traffic violations are tracked individually, and defensive driving courses that a court accepts can prevent the underlying conviction from affecting insurance renewal. The mechanism is court-driven, not state-mandated. Ask about court acceptance at your court appearance.

Approved online courses in Oregon run about 6 hours and cost around $25. Available once every 12 months. Not available for DUI or reckless driving. Where the court accepts course completion, the ticket is prevented from generating an insurance surcharge, which for the average Oregon driver looking at a three-year insurance impact is a substantial return. Oregon insurers may also offer voluntary discounts for course completion; verify with your carrier.

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Can I take defensive driving online in Oregon?**
Yes. Oregon courts accept approved online defensive driving courses for ticket dismissal on eligible violations.

**How long is Oregon defensive driving?**
Approved online courses run about 6 hours.

**How much does Oregon defensive driving cost?**
Course tuition typically runs $19.95 to $30 for approved online providers.

**Does Oregon defensive driving dismiss my ticket?**
When the court accepts course completion, yes. Oregon does not use a traditional demerit point system, so the effective outcome is preventing the underlying conviction from affecting insurance renewal. Ask about court acceptance at your court appearance.

**How often can I take Oregon defensive driving?**
Once every 12 months for court-approved dismissal purposes.

**Can I take Oregon defensive driving for a DUI or reckless driving charge?**
No. Oregon defensive driving is not available for DUI, reckless driving, or serious traffic violations. It is intended for minor moving violations only.

## Pennsylvania

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/pennsylvania

Pennsylvania has no voluntary online course that dismisses a ticket or takes points off your record. When a driver reaches six or more points, or is caught going 31 or more mph over the limit, PennDOT assigns a mandatory Driver Improvement School. Completing that six-hour course is a requirement, not a way to clear a ticket, and it does not remove points. Points come off over time as your record stays clean. Contact PennDOT or the court printed on your citation to learn what applies to you. Last checked August 2026.

**Source:** PennDOT Driver Improvement School (FS-DIS)

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Estimated all-in cost of a first speeding ticket:** $1,494 (fine plus a three-year insurance surcharge; 2026 study at https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket)

**Does an online course dismiss a ticket or remove points in Pennsylvania?**
No. Pennsylvania has no voluntary online course that dismisses a ticket or removes points. PennDOT assigns a mandatory Driver Improvement School to certain drivers, and completing it is a requirement, not a way to clear a ticket.

**Who has to take the Pennsylvania Driver Improvement School?**
Drivers who reach six or more points, or who are cited at 31 or more mph over the limit; PennDOT assigns the six-hour course (PennDOT FS-DIS).

**How do points come off my Pennsylvania record?**
With time and a clean record. No voluntary course removes them. For your ticket, contact PennDOT or the court on your citation.

## South Carolina

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/south-carolina

South Carolina does not dismiss tickets through traffic school. Its benefit is a four-point reduction, but it is tied to one specific course: the National Safety Council eight-hour defensive driving course, taken in a classroom or the NSC virtual format (S.C. Code § 56-1-770). General online defensive driving courses do not qualify for the reduction, which is why we do not list a partner offer here. Choose from the SCDMV-approved NSC options, and remember the reduction lowers points rather than dismissing the ticket. Last checked August 2026.

**Source:** S.C. Code § 56-1-770; SCDMV

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Can I take the South Carolina point-reduction course online?**
Only in the National Safety Council classroom or NSC virtual format. General online defensive driving courses do not qualify for the four-point reduction, which is why we list no partner offer here. Choose from the SCDMV-approved NSC options.

**How many points does the South Carolina course remove?**
Four points, once, for completing the NSC eight-hour course (S.C. Code § 56-1-770).

## South Dakota

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/south-dakota

South Dakota has no statewide traffic-school program that dismisses a ticket or takes points off your record. The state does keep a point count, and a license is suspended at 15 points in 12 months or 22 in 24 months, but points come off only with time, not with a course. A court can, uncommonly, allow an approved course toward a dismissal at its own discretion, so ask the court printed on your citation whether that is possible before you enroll. Last checked August 2026.

**Source:** South Dakota DPS Driver Licensing; point-suspension thresholds (15 points in 12 months or 22 in 24 months)

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Does traffic school dismiss a ticket in South Dakota?**
There is no statewide program that does, and South Dakota courts do not commonly grant a course-based dismissal. You can ask the court on your citation whether it will consider one, but do not count on it.

**Can a course reduce points in South Dakota?**
No. South Dakota keeps a point count and suspends a license at 15 points in 12 months or 22 in 24 months, but no course removes points; they come off only with time.

**Is there any online traffic school benefit in South Dakota?**
Not a statewide one. An approved course can still improve your driving, and some insurers offer a voluntary discount, but that is up to the insurer. For your ticket, ask the clerk of the court printed on your citation.
