## Texas

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/texas

Texas drivers cited for most non-CDL moving violations under 25 mph over the limit can request a TDLR-approved 6-hour Driving Safety Course (DSC) to dismiss the ticket and keep the conviction off their record, under Code of Criminal Procedure art. 45A.352. The driver must request the court's permission before the appearance date, plead guilty or no contest, present a valid Texas license and proof of liability insurance, and complete the course within 90 days. On completion the charge is dismissed and no conviction is reported to the driving record; many insurers also give a defensive-driving discount, though Texas has no state-mandated discount. The DSC dismissal is available once every 12 months per driver, and is not available to commercial license holders or for violations 25-plus mph over the limit, in construction zones with workers present, or for passing a stopped school bus. (Deferred disposition is a separate remedy: a court-ordered probation period under Chapter 45A, not the course election.) Texas SB 296, effective September 1, 2025, lets multiple citations from the same traffic stop each be dismissed. Last checked August 2026.

**Source:** Tex. Code Crim. Proc. art. 45A.352; TDLR 6-hour driving safety course

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Estimated all-in cost of a first speeding ticket:** $5,047 (fine plus a three-year insurance surcharge; 2026 study at https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket)

**How often can I use Texas defensive driving for ticket dismissal?**
Once per 12 months. You cannot use a driving safety course dismissal if you have already done so within the past 12 months. The violation also cannot be more than 25 mph over the posted limit.

**Can I do Texas defensive driving online?**
Yes. TDLR-approved online defensive driving courses are accepted by Texas courts. Always verify your provider is listed on the TDLR website before enrolling.

**Does Texas defensive driving dismiss my ticket?**
Yes, through a driving safety course (DSC) dismissal under Code of Criminal Procedure art. 45A.352. You request the court's permission, plead guilty or no contest, pay a court fee, and complete a 6-hour DSC within 90 days; the charge is then dismissed and no conviction is reported. Deferred disposition is a different remedy, a court-ordered probation period, so ask the court which one applies.

**How long is Texas defensive driving?**
Six hours, the shortest state-mandated course length in the country. It is five hours of instruction plus one hour of mandatory breaks.

**Who submits my certificate to the Texas court?**
You do. After completing the course you receive a certificate and submit it, with a certified copy of your Texas driving record, to the court by the deadline in your dismissal order (usually 90 days from the plea date).

## Utah

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/utah

Utah does not dismiss tickets through traffic school; the course benefit is a point reduction. Completing an approved defensive driving course reduces points on your record through the Utah DLD points system. Keeping the conviction off your record is a separate court process called a plea in abeyance, arranged with the court rather than earned by a course. So a course lowers points, while dismissal runs through the court. Last checked August 2026.

**Source:** Utah DLD Points System

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Estimated all-in cost of a first speeding ticket:** $1,792 (fine plus a three-year insurance surcharge; 2026 study at https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket)

**Does traffic school dismiss a ticket in Utah?**
No. The course benefit is a point reduction through the Utah DLD points system. Keeping a conviction off your record is a separate court process, a plea in abeyance, not something the course earns.

**What is a plea in abeyance in Utah?**
A court arrangement, separate from any course, that can keep the conviction off your record if you meet the court's conditions. Ask the court on your citation whether you qualify.

**How long is the Utah defensive driving course?**
Four hours (Utah DLD Points System).

## Vermont

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/vermont

Vermont does not currently accept online defensive driving courses for ticket dismissal or point reduction. The state's driver improvement programs are in-person only, generally assigned by the DMV rather than voluntarily elected.

Vermont is the cheapest state in America for a first speeding ticket, with an all-in cost of about $1,305 (fine plus three-year insurance surcharge). The relative affordability limits the financial return on any relief mechanism. For a Vermont driver looking at a routine moving violation, the primary options are contesting the ticket at court or accepting the underlying penalty. Online defensive driving isn't a legitimate option in Vermont. Any provider claiming otherwise for VT drivers should be avoided.

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Estimated all-in cost of a first speeding ticket:** $1,305 (fine plus a three-year insurance surcharge; 2026 study at https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket)

**Can I take defensive driving online in Vermont?**
No. Vermont does not accept online defensive driving courses for ticket dismissal or point reduction. Any provider claiming otherwise for Vermont drivers is not offering a legitimate course.

**What driver improvement options does Vermont offer?**
Vermont's driver improvement programs are in-person only, generally assigned by the DMV rather than voluntarily elected.

**Why is Vermont so different from other states on this?**
Vermont is one of a small group of New England states (along with Maine, Massachusetts, and New Hampshire) that does not accept online defensive driving for standard driver relief.

**What are the financial stakes for a Vermont ticket?**
Vermont is the cheapest state in America for a first speeding ticket, with an all-in cost of about $1,305 (fine plus three-year insurance surcharge). The relative affordability limits the financial return on any relief mechanism.

**How can I reduce the insurance impact of a Vermont ticket?**
The primary options are contesting the ticket at court or accepting the underlying penalty. Online defensive driving isn't a legitimate option in Vermont.

## Virginia

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/virginia

Virginia operates a unique two-direction point system administered by the DMV: drivers accumulate demerit points for violations and earn safe driving points for clean years (one per year, capped at five). Voluntarily completing an 8-hour DMV-approved Driver Improvement Clinic credits 5 safe driving points to your record once every 24 months under Va. Code §§46.2-489 and 46.2-498, with the clinic capped at $100. Important caveat: the safe-driving-points credit and the insurance-discount benefit are mutually exclusive — you must declare your purpose at registration and choose one. The DMV-issued Online Driver Improvement Clinic Certificate (Form DIC 552B) is the only document the courts and DMV will accept as proof of completion. Court-ordered clinic attendance — required for drivers who accumulate excessive demerit points or as part of sentencing — must be completed within 90 days or the driver's license will be suspended; the court determines whether safe-driving points are awarded for court-ordered completions. CDL holders cannot receive demerit-point relief through the clinic for offenses committed in commercial vehicles.

**Source:** Virginia DMV Driver Improvement Clinic, eight-hour classroom sessions (Va. Code § 46.2-490.2; dmv.virginia.gov)

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Estimated all-in cost of a first speeding ticket:** $1,818 (fine plus a three-year insurance surcharge; 2026 study at https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket)

**Does Virginia driver improvement dismiss my ticket?**
Not by itself. Completing a DMV-approved Driver Improvement Clinic reduces your demerit points by five and earns a mandatory insurance discount, but on its own it does not dismiss the ticket or remove the conviction. Separately, some Virginia courts offer deferred disposition, where the judge may dismiss the charge if you complete an approved course — that is decided court by court, so confirm with the court on your citation.

**Who submits my certificate in Virginia?**
Your school submits completion to the Virginia DMV, which processes the 5-point reduction automatically. You submit the certificate to your insurance company separately to receive the discount.

**How long is Virginia driver improvement?**
Virginia Driver Improvement Clinic (DIC) courses are 8 hours.

**Can I do Virginia driver improvement online?**
Yes. Virginia DMV-approved online Driver Improvement Clinics are accepted statewide, and you can complete the full 8-hour course online at your own pace.

**How often can I do Virginia driver improvement?**
Once every 12 months for the demerit point reduction benefit. The auto insurance discount typically lasts 3 years from the date of completion.

## Washington

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/washington

Washington keeps no point total on your license, and no online course automatically erases a ticket. What can clear one is a court-granted deferred finding. Under RCW 46.63.070(5), the court may defer a moving-violation infraction once every seven years and set the conditions it thinks appropriate. Many courts choose to require a traffic safety course as one of those conditions, but whether a course is required at all, and which one counts, is the court's decision. If you meet the conditions through the deferral period, the court may dismiss the infraction. Commercial-license holders and anyone driving a commercial vehicle at the time are not eligible. Ask the court printed on your citation what it requires before you enroll in anything. Last checked August 2026.

**Source:** RCW 46.63.070(5)

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Can traffic school dismiss a ticket in Washington?**
Not on its own. The route to a dismissal is a court-granted deferred finding: under RCW 46.63.070(5) the court may defer a moving-violation infraction once every seven years and set the conditions it deems appropriate. Many courts choose to require a traffic safety course, but whether a course is required, and which one, is the court's decision. If you meet the conditions, the court may dismiss the infraction at the end of the deferral period.

**How often can I get a deferred finding in Washington?**
Once every seven years for a moving violation, and separately once every seven years for a nonmoving violation. Commercial-license holders and anyone driving a commercial vehicle at the time are excluded (RCW 46.63.070(5)).

**Does Washington have a driver-point system?**
No. Washington keeps no point total on your license. For your ticket, ask the court printed on your citation whether it will grant a deferred finding and what conditions it sets.

## Washington DC

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/washington-dc

Washington DC runs an official online traffic school through the DC DMV. If a DMV hearing examiner approves it, completing a DC DMV-approved online course removes points from your driving record. You have 30 days from the hearing decision to finish, and the two approved online providers are the American Safety Council and Online Traffic School Inc. This is a point-removal program, not a dismissal: the ticket conviction itself still stands. Ask the DC DMV about a hearing before you enroll. Last checked August 2026.

**Source:** DC DMV Online Traffic School (dmv.dc.gov/service/dc-dmv-online-traffic-school); DC DMV Driver Point System

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Does DC have online traffic school?**
Yes. The DC DMV runs an official online traffic school. With prior approval from a DMV hearing examiner, completing a DC DMV-approved online course removes points from your driving record. The two approved online providers are the American Safety Council and Online Traffic School Inc.

**Does DC traffic school dismiss my ticket?**
No. It removes points from your record, but the ticket conviction still stands. In DC this is a point-removal program, not a dismissal, and you still pay the fine.

**How do I qualify for DC's online traffic school?**
You need approval from a DC DMV hearing examiner first. Once approved, you complete the DMV-approved online course within 30 days of the hearing decision. Contact the DC DMV about a hearing before enrolling.

**Which online providers are approved in DC?**
The DC DMV lists two approved online providers for its traffic school: the American Safety Council and Online Traffic School Inc. Confirm the current list with the DC DMV before you pay.

## Wisconsin

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/wisconsin

Wisconsin drivers can reduce up to 3 demerit points from their driving record by completing a WisDOT-approved Traffic Safety School course, governed by Wis. Admin. Code Trans 101.07. The student has 30 days from completion to notify the DMV to apply the credit, and the option is available only once every 3 years. Wisconsin's demerit point system is built around a rolling 12-month window — only points accumulated in the prior 12 months count toward suspension, with 12+ points triggering a license suspension. If your license is already suspended for accumulating 12 to 14 points, completing the course can lift the suspension. A separate 2-hour Failure to Yield Right-of-Way course is mandatory after a failure-to-yield conviction; it satisfies that specific requirement but does not reduce points. OWI (impaired driving) courses are a separate track entirely.

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Who submits my certificate in Wisconsin?**
For the DMV-mandated Failure to Yield course, your provider submits completion electronically to the Wisconsin DMV. For general traffic school ticket dismissal, you receive a certificate and submit it to your court directly.

**How long is Wisconsin traffic school?**
The Wisconsin Failure to Yield course is 2 hours (state-mandated). General traffic school for ticket dismissal is typically 4 hours, depending on the court's requirements.

**How often can I do Wisconsin traffic school?**
No fixed statewide cooldown for general ticket dismissal — each court sets its own rules. For the DMV-mandated Failure to Yield course, this is a one-time requirement triggered by conviction.

**Can I do Wisconsin traffic school online?**
Yes. Online courses are accepted in Wisconsin for both the Failure to Yield requirement and general traffic school ticket dismissal.

**Does Wisconsin traffic school dismiss my ticket?**
Court-by-court for most violations. The Wisconsin DOT also mandates a specific Failure to Yield course for drivers convicted of that violation. For other minor violations, contact your court to confirm eligibility and get permission before enrolling.

## Wyoming

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/wyoming

Wyoming does not use a driver point system — the Wyoming Department of Transportation (WYDOT) tracks moving-violation convictions by count rather than numeric points, and four moving-violation convictions within any 12-month period trigger an automatic 90-day license suspension under Title 31 of the Wyoming Statutes. Whether traffic school can dismiss a ticket is decided court by court at the circuit court or municipal court level, typically as part of a diversion or deferred-prosecution agreement; some courts accept WyDOT-recognized online defensive driving providers, others do not. CDL holders are generally excluded, as are violations involving 25-plus mph over the limit, school zones, accidents, reckless driving, or DUI. Convictions remain on the driving record for three years from the conviction date. Always contact the issuing court before enrolling in any course — Wyoming has no statewide ticket-dismissal program, and a defensive driving certificate accepted by Laramie Municipal Court may not be accepted by Cheyenne or Casper. Last checked August 2026.

**Last verified:** August 2026

**Does Wyoming have a driver license point system?**
No. Wyoming does not use a numeric driver license point system. Instead, the Wyoming Department of Transportation (WyDOT) tracks the count of moving-violation convictions on a driving record. Four moving-violation convictions within any 12-month period trigger an automatic 90-day license suspension under Title 31 of the Wyoming Statutes; each subsequent violation can extend the suspension by another 90 days.

**Can I take an online defensive driving course to dismiss a Wyoming traffic ticket?**
Sometimes — eligibility depends entirely on which court issued the ticket. Wyoming has no statewide diversion program, so each circuit court and municipal court decides whether to accept a defensive driving completion certificate as a basis for dismissal. Some courts accept WyDOT-recognized online providers; others require an in-person class or do not offer dismissal at all. Contact the court listed on your citation before enrolling.

**Who is not eligible for ticket dismissal through traffic school in Wyoming?**
Most courts that allow traffic-school dismissal exclude commercial driver's license (CDL) holders, drivers cited for speeding 25+ mph over the posted limit, violations in school zones, violations involving accidents, reckless driving, and DUI. The exact exclusion list is set by each court, so confirm with the court that issued your citation.

**How long do traffic violations stay on a Wyoming driving record?**
Traffic conviction records remain on a Wyoming driving record for 3 years from the date of conviction. During that time the conviction can be combined with new violations to trigger the 4-in-12-months suspension threshold, and insurance carriers can typically see the conviction during the rate-setting period.

**Does Wyoming require insurance carriers to give a discount for completing a defensive driving course?**
Wyoming does not statutorily mandate insurance discounts for completing a defensive driving course. Whether your carrier offers a discount, and how much, is up to the individual insurer — contact your auto insurance agent before enrolling if an insurance discount is your primary goal.

**What happens if I get four traffic tickets in 12 months in Wyoming?**
WyDOT will automatically suspend your driver's license for 90 days. The suspension extends by an additional 90 days for each subsequent moving-violation conviction. Because Wyoming uses a violation-count system rather than points, even minor speeding tickets count toward the threshold — there's no equivalent of a low-point violation that doesn't add up.

---

## Aceable Review

Aceable is the one traffic school that actually feels built this decade. It started as a mobile app, not a desktop course someone bolted an app onto later, and you can tell. # TrafficSchoolPicker.com — State Question Pages

> Per-state answers to common traffic-school questions, each verified against primary sources.
> Source: TrafficSchoolPicker editorial content, verified against official DMV, court, and statute records.

## Can You Take Defensive Driving Online in Arizona?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/arizona/can-you-take-traffic-school-online

- **Online accepted:** Yes, fully, by every Arizona court, for schools certified by the Arizona Supreme Court
- **The credential:** Supreme Court certification, not MVD approval, is what makes an Arizona school real
- **Your school reports for you:** Completion goes to the court electronically within 24 hours
- **The deadline is yours alone:** Course complete at least 7 days before your court date
- **Last verified:** August 2026

Yes, completely. Online defensive driving is accepted by every Arizona court for the diversion program, and the state built the plumbing to match: your school transmits your completion to the court electronically within 24 hours of finishing, no certificate to mail, no clerk visit.

The credential to check is distinctive here. Arizona's program is run by the Arizona Supreme Court, not the MVD, and the court certifies each school and each delivery method. A school that's legitimate for Arizona will hold and display that Supreme Court certification, and Arizona is unusually strict about what gets certified, requiring online curricula to be substantially distinct rather than relicensed copies of one another. If a site can't show Arizona Supreme Court certification, its certificate is worthless here regardless of how many other states approve it.

Format settled, the two rules that actually decide outcomes are timing rules: eligibility runs once every 12 months measured violation date to violation date, and your course must be done at least 7 days before your court date. The online course being available at midnight in your kitchen is exactly why the 7-day rule catches people; available-anytime breeds started-too-late.

Every Supreme Court-certified online school we track is compared on the Arizona page, what completion buys, full dismissal, nothing reported to insurers, is on our points page, and the fee layers are on our cost page.

**Sources:** last verified 2026-08-13 | ARS 28-3392 | ACJA 7-205 | azcourts.gov

---

## Does Defensive Driving Remove Points in Arizona?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/arizona/does-traffic-school-remove-points

- **Points removed:** None needed. Completing the course means the citation is dismissed and no points are ever assessed
- **What insurers see:** Nothing. The violation is not reported, so there is no conviction to price
- **Legal basis:** Arizona Defensive Driving Program under ARS §28-3392, administered by the Arizona Supreme Court
- **Frequency:** Once every 12 months, measured violation date to violation date
- **Deadline:** Complete the course at least 7 days before your court date
- **How the court finds out:** Your school submits completion electronically within 24 hours
- **CDL holders:** Eligible only if the violation occurred in a non-commercial vehicle
- **Not eligible:** Violations involving a collision with serious injury or death
- **Course:** 4 to 4.5 hours, Supreme Court-certified school; typical cost $45 to $150 plus state and court fees
- **Last verified:** August 2026

Arizona makes the question obsolete. There are no points to remove because, done right, the points never happen and neither does anything else.

Here's the machine. Arizona's Defensive Driving Program is a diversion program, run not by the MVD but by the Arizona Supreme Court, which certifies every school. Get an eligible ticket, complete a certified course before your deadline, and the citation is dismissed. Not reduced, not masked, not credited against. Dismissed, with no points assessed and nothing reported for insurers to see. California hides the conviction; Texas erases the charge after a plea. Arizona intercepts the whole thing before it becomes anything. It's the cleanest version of this mechanism in the United States.

The program's demands in exchange are mostly about the calendar. You can use it once every 12 months, measured violation date to violation date. And the deadline that matters isn't your court date, it's 7 days before your court date, which is when your course must be complete. Arizona drivers lose this program to that one-week buffer constantly, because they diarize the court date and start the course the weekend before. Count back seven days, then give yourself margin. Your school transmits your completion to the court electronically within 24 hours, so the follow-through is automatic once you finish; the finishing on time is entirely on you.

Eligibility is broad with sharp edges. Minor civil moving violations qualify. Violations from a collision involving serious injury or death don't. CDL holders, shut out entirely in most states, get a carve-out here: eligible as long as the violation happened in a non-commercial vehicle. The course itself is short by national standards, 4 to 4.5 hours by rule, though Arizona's pricing runs higher than most states, $45 to $150 in tuition before state and court fees, because the diversion fee structure rides along with the course.

And it's worth every dollar of that. Our Arizona data puts a typical 10-over ticket at a $231 fine and roughly $3,039 in three-year insurance exposure as a ceiling estimate. The diversion deletes both: the fine goes with the dismissed citation and the insurance exposure never materializes because there's no conviction to rate. Very few financial decisions return three thousand dollars for one afternoon, and Arizona hands it to eligible drivers once a year.

Arizona's program follows the citation and the court rather than your home state, so [drivers licensed elsewhere](https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/out-of-state-ticket) can often use it for an Arizona ticket. Because eligibility is set by the court on your citation, out-of-state drivers should confirm with that court before enrolling.

Every Arizona Supreme Court-certified online school we track is compared on the Arizona page.

**Sources:** last verified 2026-08-13 | ARS 28-3392 | AZ Supreme Court Defensive Driving Program: https://www.azcourts.gov/ | AZDOT: https://azdot.gov/motor-vehicles/driver-services/defensive-driving | Ticket Cost Study: https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket

---

## How Long Is Defensive Driving School in Arizona?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/arizona/how-long-does-traffic-school-take

- **Course length:** 4 to 4.5 hours, and uniquely, the 4.5 is a maximum, set by the Arizona Supreme Court
- **Shortest course in our coverage, attached to the biggest benefit:** full dismissal
- **The deadline around it:** Complete at least 7 days before your court date
- **Last verified:** August 2026

Four to four and a half hours, and Arizona is the only state in our coverage that caps the course from above: Supreme Court program rules set a minimum of 4 hours and a maximum of 4.5, excluding breaks and registration. Nobody can sell you a padded 8-hour Arizona diversion course, because one isn't allowed to exist.

That makes Arizona's trade the steepest in the country in the driver's favor: the shortest mandatory sit anywhere, exchanged for the biggest prize anywhere, complete dismissal of the citation with no points and nothing reported to insurers. Four and a half hours against roughly three thousand dollars of avoided insurance exposure is the arithmetic; there's no version of being too busy for it that survives contact with that number.

The hours themselves are schedulable online with saved progress, certified schools transmit your completion to the court electronically within 24 hours of finishing, and the only clock that can beat you is the one outside the course: everything must be done at least 7 days before your court date. Count back seven days from the date on your citation paperwork, then subtract your own procrastination honestly, and start.

Every Arizona Supreme Court-certified online school we track is compared on the Arizona page, and the full diversion mechanics are on our points page.

**Sources:** last verified 2026-08-13 | azcourts.gov | ARS 28-3392

---

## How Much Does Defensive Driving School Cost in Arizona?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/arizona/how-much-does-traffic-school-cost

- **Course tuition:** Roughly $38.95 to $150 depending on school; Improv listed at $38.95 as of August 2026
- **Tuition is not the total:** Arizona adds a state fee and a court diversion fee on top, set per court, so the all-in number varies by where you got the ticket
- **What the total buys:** Complete dismissal of the citation, no points, nothing reported to insurers
- **The ticket you're deleting:** A typical 10-over ticket runs a $231 fine and roughly $3,039 in three-year insurance exposure (ceiling estimate), and the diversion removes both
- **Deadline that matters:** Course complete at least 7 days before your court date
- **Last verified:** August 2026

Arizona's course is the most expensive in this series, and it's also the only one where the price doesn't really matter, because of what's on the other side of the trade.

Start with the structure, because Arizona bills differently from every other state we cover. What you pay has three layers: the school's tuition, a state fee, and a diversion fee set by the court that issued your ticket. Tuition alone runs roughly $38.95 to $150 depending on the school, Improv listed at $38.95 in our August 2026 pull, but the checkout total will be meaningfully higher once the court and state charges attach, and that total varies by jurisdiction because each court sets its own diversion fee. That's why Arizona schools can't advertise one clean price and why you should compare schools on tuition, the only layer they control, then expect the same government fees regardless of which school you pick.

Now the other side of the trade. Completing the course means the citation is dismissed. Not points reduced, dismissed: no fine, no points assessed, no conviction, nothing for your insurer to ever see. Our Arizona data puts a typical 10-over ticket at a $231 fine plus roughly $3,039 in three-year insurance exposure as a ceiling estimate, and the diversion deletes the entire column. Even at the top of the market, a $150 course plus court fees returning three thousand dollars of avoided cost is the best-value purchase on this entire site. Arizona drivers who are eligible and skip it because the checkout total looked high compared to other states are making a $3,000 mistake to save $100.

Two cost-adjacent rules to respect: the program is available once every 12 months, measured violation date to violation date, so its value is rationed, and your course must be complete at least 7 days before your court date, so its value expires. The most expensive version of this course is the one you start too late.

Every Arizona Supreme Court-certified online school we track is compared on the Arizona page, and the full diversion mechanics are on our points page.

**Sources:** Ticket Cost Study: https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket | ARS 28-3392 | AZ Supreme Court: https://www.azcourts.gov/

## How Often Can You Take Defensive Driving in Arizona?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/arizona/how-often-can-you-take-traffic-school

- **Diversion frequency:** Once every 12 months, measured violation date to violation date
- **The measurement matters:** It's the dates of the two violations that must be 12+ months apart
- **Each use still requires:** Course complete at least 7 days before that ticket's court date
- **Last verified:** August 2026

Once every 12 months, and Arizona measures the interval more precisely than any state we cover: violation date to violation date.

Here's why the measurement is the whole answer. Arizona's diversion dismisses the citation entirely, so the state rations it tightly and defines the ration exactly: the date of the violation you want diverted must be more than 12 months after the date of the last violation you diverted. Not the course dates, not the court dates, the violation dates. Two tickets 13 months apart both qualify no matter when you took each course; two tickets 11 months apart never can, even if the first course was 14 months ago. When a new ticket lands, the eligibility check is one subtraction between two dates printed on two citations.

That precision creates a genuinely awkward edge case worth knowing: a driver who diverted a ticket in, say, September 2025 and picks up another in July 2026 is simply outside the program for that new ticket. There's no partial credit and no discretion in the interval. The options revert to what any ineligible driver has, contesting or paying, which is why the once-a-year dismissal deserves to be treated like the valuable, rationed thing it is rather than an assumed safety net.

And each eligible use carries its own internal deadline: the course must be complete at least 7 days before that ticket's court date. The annual ration and the 7-day rule fail people in opposite directions, one from using the program too often, one from starting it too late.

What a successful use buys, the full dismissal with nothing reported to insurers, is on our points page, the fee structure is on our cost page, and every Supreme Court-certified online school we track is compared on the Arizona page.

**Sources:** last verified 2026-08-13 | ARS 28-3392 | azcourts.gov

## Is Defensive Driving Worth It in Arizona?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/arizona/is-traffic-school-worth-it

- **Verdict:** The strongest yes on this site
- **What you spend:** Roughly $38.95 to $150 tuition plus state and court fees, and 4 to 4.5 hours
- **What it deletes:** The citation itself, the $231 fine, and roughly $3,039 in three-year insurance exposure (ceiling estimate), around a 20x return even at the top of the fee range
- **The only ways to lose it:** Miss the 7-day deadline or be inside the 12-month window
- **Last verified:** August 2026

Yes, more decisively than anywhere else in the country, because Arizona is the only state where the course deletes the entire problem.

Everywhere else, some residue survives: California's fine, New York's conviction, Georgia's insurer-visible record. Arizona's diversion leaves nothing. Complete the course before the deadline and the citation is dismissed, the $231 fine is never owed, no points are assessed, and nothing is reported for insurers to price, taking the roughly $3,039 three-year exposure at ceiling off the table with it. Total avoided value runs past $3,200 on a typical ticket. Against even the top of the market, $150 tuition plus the state and court fees your jurisdiction stacks on, that's on the order of a 20x return, and at the cheaper schools it climbs well beyond. Four and a half hours is the entire time cost, the shortest course in our coverage.

The worth-it question in Arizona therefore collapses into an eligibility question. Once every 12 months, measured violation date to violation date; nothing involving serious injury; CDL only for tickets in a personal vehicle. Eligible and past those gates, the only remaining way to lose value is the calendar: the course must be complete at least 7 days before your court date, and every year Arizona drivers donate three-thousand-dollar returns to procrastination.

If you're eligible, this isn't a decision, it's a deadline. Certified schools are compared on the Arizona page, and the 7-day mechanics are on our frequency page.

**Sources:** Ticket Cost Study: https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket | ARS 28-3392

## Can You Do Traffic School Online in California?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/california/can-you-take-traffic-school-online

- **Online accepted:** Yes. DMV-licensed internet traffic schools are accepted by California courts
- **How to confirm a school is real:** The DMV's traffic school list, searchable by name, shows every licensed school and its status
- **Not eligible at any format:** CDL holders (for masking)
- **Last verified:** August 2026

Yes. California licenses internet traffic schools as their own DMV category, and courts accept them the same as classroom schools. Online is how the overwhelming majority of California traffic school gets done.

The question worth your thirty seconds isn't whether online counts, it's whether the specific school does. California's market has hundreds of licensed schools and a fringe of unlicensed lookalikes, and the DMV settles it definitively: its public traffic school list is searchable by business name and shows every licensed school, its license number, and whether the license is active. Any legitimate school will also display its license number on its site. If you can't find a school on the DMV list, spend your money elsewhere.

Eligibility rides on the ticket, not the format: your court notice controls whether you can attend at all, the once-per-18-months masking window applies online or off, and commercial license holders are excluded either way.

Every school we compare on the California page is DMV-licensed with the license verified, and the fee stack is on our cost page.

**Sources:** DMV OLL traffic school lookup | VC 1808.7

## Does Traffic School Remove Points in California?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/california/does-traffic-school-remove-points

- **Points removed by traffic school:** None. California masks the conviction instead
- **Legal mechanism:** Confidential conviction under Vehicle Code §1808.7; election under VC §41501 and Rule of Court 4.104
- **What insurers see:** Nothing. The conviction is held confidential from insurers during the masking period
- **What the DMV keeps:** The conviction stays on the internal DMV record for state purposes
- **Frequency limit:** Once per 18 months, measured from violation date to violation date
- **Eligible:** One-point moving violations, valid non-commercial California license
- **Not eligible:** Speeding 25+ mph over the limit, alcohol or drug offenses, any offense in a commercial vehicle
- **Course length:** 8 hours minimum, DMV-licensed provider
- **Typical total cost:** Fine + court administrative fee (typically $52–$55) + course tuition ($15–$45)
- **Last verified:** August 2026

No. And the distinction actually matters, because what California does instead is better.

Traffic school in California doesn't reach into your record and delete a point. It stops the point from ever becoming visible in the first place. Complete a DMV-licensed course after an eligible ticket and the court reports your conviction as confidential under Vehicle Code 1808.7. The conviction still exists. The DMV still has it. But it's held confidential from insurance companies, which means the one party you were worried about never sees it. People call this masking, and it's the cleanest version of this mechanism in any state.

That's also why timing matters so much. Masking works on the reporting step, before the conviction hits the public record. Once a conviction has been reported publicly, traffic school can't pull it back. You elect traffic school through the court before or at the time you resolve the ticket, not after.

Who qualifies. You need a valid non-commercial California license and an eligible one-point moving violation. The standard exclusions: speeding 25 mph or more over the limit, anything alcohol or drug related, and any offense committed in a commercial vehicle, whatever class of license you hold. And you get this once every 18 months, measured from violation date to violation date. Get a second eligible ticket 14 months after the first one and you're taking the point.

What it costs. Three pieces. You pay the full fine on the ticket, that doesn't go away. The court adds an administrative fee, typically $52 to $55 depending on the county. Then the course itself, and California's course market is the cheapest in the country, generally $15 to $45 for the 8-hour minimum.

What it saves. Our ticket cost data puts California's three-year insurance exposure for a routine 10-mph-over ticket at roughly $5,385 on top of a $234 fine, and that's a ceiling estimate since some carriers taper after year one. Spending under $100 to keep a conviction invisible to the people who set that number is about the best trade a California driver ever gets offered.

One thing that trips people up. Your DMV printout can still show the violation, because the record isn't erased, it's held confidential from insurers. Courts and law enforcement see it. The state counts it internally. If someone tells you their masked ticket "showed up," that's usually what happened. The masking did its job. The job was never to make it vanish for everyone.

One caveat we can't close: masking is documented to protect your California record. Whether it also stops the conviction reaching [a license issued in another state](https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/out-of-state-ticket) is genuinely unresolved — so if you're not a California licensee, don't assume traffic school here buys you the same protection.

Every school on our California page is on the DMV's licensed list and submits your certificate electronically, and we've compared what they actually cost and what they're like to get through.

**Sources:** Vehicle Code 1808.7 and 41501: https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov | Rule of Court 4.104: https://courts.ca.gov | CA DMV TVS program: https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/driver-education-and-safety/educational-resources/traffic-violator-school/ | Ticket Cost Study: https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket

## How Long Is Traffic School in California?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/california/how-long-does-traffic-school-take

- **Course length:** 8 hours is California's standard, set by the state, identical at every licensed school
- **Last verified:** August 2026

Eight hours is the standard, and it's California's number, not the school's. Every DMV-licensed traffic school teaches to the same state requirement, which is why "fastest California traffic school" ads are selling something the license doesn't permit.

The online wrinkle is that California regulates internet courses by content volume rather than a running timer, mandating the amount of material a licensed course must contain. Practically, that means your real completion time tracks your reading speed: quick readers genuinely finish faster than the nominal eight hours, slow readers take longer, and the final exam waits at the end either way. It's the one state where "how long does it take" honestly answers "how fast do you read."

The deadline around the course comes from your court: your notice sets the completion date, and the school reports electronically once you pass. Between saved progress and the court's window, the sane pattern is a few sittings, not a marathon.

Every DMV-licensed online school we track is compared on the California page, and the once-per-18-months rule on using it is on our frequency page.

**Sources:** 13 CCR 345.30 | DMV TVS program

## How Much Does Traffic School Cost in California?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/california/how-much-does-traffic-school-cost

- **Course price:** $5 to $29 online across DMV-licensed schools we track
- **Court administrative fee:** Typically $52 to $55, set by your county court
- **The fine:** You pay it in full; traffic school doesn't reduce it
- **Course length:** 8 hours minimum, DMV-licensed provider
- **Typical all-in:** Fine + roughly $60 to $85 in fee and tuition
- **What it buys:** The conviction stays confidential from insurers (VC §1808.7 masking)
- **Last verified:** August 2026

California has the cheapest traffic school courses in America and the most misleading sticker prices, because the course is the smallest number on the bill.

Three pieces. First, the fine, and you pay all of it. Traffic school in California doesn't reduce or dismiss the ticket, it masks the conviction from insurers. A typical 10-over ticket runs $234 with assessments. Second, the court's administrative fee for the traffic school option, typically $52 to $55 depending on the county. That fee usually costs more than the course. Third, tuition, and here the market has raced to the bottom in your favor: among schools we track, 5DollarTrafficSchool is genuinely five dollars and has been since 1998, Improv runs $24.95, Aceable $29. All of them cover the same 8-hour DMV minimum, because the state sets the curriculum floor, not the school.

So the honest arithmetic on a typical ticket: $234 fine, call it $54 to the court, $5 to $29 for the course. Roughly $300 all-in, of which the part you get to shop is under thirty bucks.

Which raises the fair question of whether $300 is worth it. Our California data says it isn't close. The three-year insurance exposure on that same 10-over conviction is roughly $5,385 as a ceiling estimate, because California insurers price visible convictions hard. Masking keeps the conviction confidential from them under Vehicle Code 1808.7. You're spending about $85 above the fine you owed anyway to take a four-figure risk off the table.

One warning on the cheap end. A $5 sticker sometimes grows fees at checkout, so read the final total before you pay. The schools we list on the California page are compared on the checkout price, not the banner.

**Sources:** VC 1808.7 / 42007: https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov | DMV TVS: https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/driver-education-and-safety/educational-resources/traffic-violator-school/ | Ticket Cost Study: https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket

## How Often Can You Go to Traffic School in California?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/california/how-often-can-you-take-traffic-school

- **For keeping a ticket confidential (masking):** Once every 18 months, measured violation date to violation date
- **CDL holders:** Not eligible for masking
- **Last verified:** August 2026

Once every 18 months, and California measures it the strict way: from the date of the violation, not the date you finished the course or the date the court signed off.

The mechanism matters here. California traffic school doesn't dismiss your ticket; under Vehicle Code 1808.7, it masks the conviction, keeping it confidential so insurers and employers pulling your record don't see it. That confidentiality is what's rationed. Pick up a second eligible violation within 18 months of the first and the court can still let you attend traffic school, some do, but the second conviction shows on your record anyway, points and all. You'd be paying tuition for the certificate, not the benefit.

So the practical questions when a new ticket arrives: what was the violation date on your last masked ticket, and is this new violation date at least 18 months after it? Your court notice will usually tell you whether you're eligible, but courts process on their own information, and if you believe you're outside the window and the notice says otherwise, that's a call to the clerk before you pay anything.

Two permanent exclusions run at any frequency: commercial license holders can't mask, and violations serious enough to be ineligible, alcohol offenses and the like, stay ineligible.

Inside the window with a fresh ticket, the course won't protect your record, so weigh the fine-plus-points reality instead. Outside it, the trade is excellent, roughly $52 to $55 in court fees plus a course that can cost under $10, details on our cost page.

Every DMV-licensed online school we track is compared on the California page.

**Sources:** VC 1808.7

## Is Traffic School Worth It in California?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/california/is-traffic-school-worth-it

- **Verdict:** Yes, emphatically, and it's the insurance masking doing the work
- **What you spend:** Course plus a court fee of about $52 to $55; total often under $90, sometimes under $70
- **What it can prevent:** Roughly $5,385 in three-year insurance exposure (ceiling estimate), a return on the order of 60x
- **What it doesn't touch:** The fine itself, around $234 all-in, which you pay either way
- **Last verified:** August 2026

Yes, and the reason is a nuance worth stating plainly: in California you pay the fine no matter what. Roughly $234 all-in on a typical ticket once the state stacks its penalty assessments on the base fine. Traffic school never touches that number. What it touches is the far bigger one.

California insurance runs high, and our data puts the three-year exposure on an unmasked ticket at roughly $5,385 as a ceiling estimate, driven by one of the steepest premium-increase percentages in the country. Masking the conviction, which is what traffic school does under VC 1808.7, keeps the ticket confidential and that exposure unrealized. Your cost for the masking: the court's administrative fee, about $52 to $55, plus a course that can run under $10 in California's hyper-competitive market. Call it $60 to $90 total. Against a $5,385 ceiling, that's a return on the order of 60x, and still excellent if your carrier's real surcharge lands well under the ceiling.

The conditions: eligibility per your court notice, once every 18 months measured violation date to violation date, no commercial licenses. Inside the 18-month window the answer flips to no; you'd be buying a course whose benefit can't apply.

## Can You Take Florida Traffic School Online?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/florida/can-you-take-traffic-school-online

- **Online accepted:** Yes, statewide, for FLHSMV-approved Basic Driver Improvement courses
- **The deadline that governs everything:** Elect the course with the clerk within 30 days of the citation
- **Not eligible at any format:** CDL holders; citations for 30+ mph over the limit
- **Last verified:** August 2026

Yes. Florida approves online Basic Driver Improvement courses at the state level, through FLHSMV, so an approved online course counts in every county; there's no court-by-court lottery on format.

What Florida rations instead is time and turns. The election, telling the clerk you're taking the course, must happen within 30 days of the citation, and blowing that deadline closes the option no matter how eligible the course is. And each election spends one of your once-per-12-months, five-per-lifetime allotment, which is worth checking on your driving record before you commit a marginal ticket to it.

The exclusions run at any format: commercial license holders can't elect, and a citation for 30 mph or more over the limit is ineligible outright.

One practical note on picking a school: FLHSMV approval is the only credential that matters. Florida's course market is crowded with lookalike sites, and the approved-provider status is what makes the certificate real. Every online BDI course we compare on the Florida page carries it, and the full price stack, including the state assessment fees behind Florida's famously low sticker prices, is on our cost page.

**Sources:** Fla. Stat. 318.14(9)

## Does Traffic School Remove Points in Florida?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/florida/does-traffic-school-remove-points

- **Points removed by traffic school:** None removed. Electing BDI prevents points from ever being assessed
- **Legal mechanism:** Election under Fla. Stat. §318.14(9); adjudication withheld, no points per §322.27
- **Is it a conviction:** No. Adjudication withheld is not a conviction (§318.14(11))
- **Insurance protection:** Insurer may not raise your premium or refuse renewal based solely on that infraction (§626.9541(1)(o))
- **Election deadline:** 30 days from the citation
- **Frequency limit:** Once per 12 months, eight elections per lifetime
- **Not eligible:** CDL or commercial permit holders, tickets in a commercial vehicle, speeding 30+ mph over the limit
- **Course:** 4-hour Basic Driver Improvement (BDI), FLHSMV-approved
- **Certificate:** School e-files with the clerk within 5 days (§318.1451)
- **Last verified:** August 2026

Florida's answer is no, and it's the best no on this site. BDI doesn't remove points. It makes sure they never exist.

Here's the mechanism. When you get an eligible ticket, you can elect a Basic Driver Improvement course instead of paying and taking the conviction. Make that election and complete the 4-hour course, and under section 318.14(9) adjudication is withheld and no points may be assessed. The statute goes further in subsection (11): adjudication withheld is not a conviction. Nothing to remove, because nothing ever landed.

The whole thing turns on the deadline. You have 30 days from the citation to make the election, and you make it with the clerk of court, before you pay, before you plead. Pay the ticket first and you've converted it into a conviction, and BDI can't touch a conviction. More Florida drivers lose this option to the calendar than to eligibility. If you're inside your 30 days right now, sort the election today and worry about picking a course after.

Florida then does something almost no other state does. Section 626.9541(1)(o) tells insurers they cannot impose an additional premium or refuse to renew your policy based solely on that infraction. Most states leave you hoping your insurer never looks. Florida makes it law.

Who's out. Anyone holding a CDL or commercial learner's permit, anyone cited while driving a commercial vehicle, and anyone clocked 30 mph or more over the limit. Notice that's 30, not the 25 you'll see quoted for California and Texas. Florida's line is more generous and half the internet gets it wrong.

You can elect once every 12 months and eight times in your life (s. 318.14(9), as amended in 2025), so treat it as a card you play, not a subscription. The clock runs ticket to ticket.

On cost, Florida's course market is absurdly cheap, $4 to $25 for the 4-hour BDI, though watch the fee stack at checkout on the bargain ones. You still pay the citation. Set that against our ticket cost data for Florida, roughly $3,966 in three-year insurance exposure on a $204 ticket as a ceiling estimate, and the election is the highest-leverage 30-day deadline in Florida driving.

Once you finish, the school files your certificate electronically with the clerk within 5 days under 318.1451. Check the county's court records portal that it landed. That's the one piece of follow-through left to you.

Florida also doesn't care where your license is from — the BDI election is open [even to drivers licensed in another state](https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/out-of-state-ticket), which is rarer than it sounds and makes Florida one of the cleaner options when you're ticketed away from home.

Every FLHSMV-approved online BDI course we track is compared on the Florida page, including which ones keep the checkout price honest.

**Sources:** Fla. Stat. 318.14 (current year): http://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0300-0399/0318/Sections/0318.14.html | 318.1451 e-filing via Polk clerk: https://polkcountyclerk.net/FAQ.aspx?QID=167 | CDL exclusion via Martin clerk: https://www.martinclerk.com/m/faq?cat=19,28 | 626.9541(1)(o): last verified 2026-08-13 | FLHSMV: https://www.flhsmv.gov/driver-licenses-id-cards/driver-improvement/ | Ticket Cost Study: https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket

## How Long Is Florida Traffic School?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/florida/how-long-does-traffic-school-take

- **Basic Driver Improvement, the ticket-election course:** 4 hours, set by the state
- **Don't confuse it with ADI:** Advanced Driver Improvement runs 8 or 12 hours and serves court orders and license reinstatement, not the standard election
- **Last verified:** August 2026

Four hours, for the course you almost certainly mean. Florida's Basic Driver Improvement, the one you elect within 30 days of a citation, is a 4-hour course by state rule, the same at every FLHSMV-approved school, making it one of the shortest ticket courses in the country.

The confusion to avoid is buying the wrong Florida course entirely. Florida also runs Advanced Driver Improvement at 8 and 12 hours, which serves court orders and habitual-offender license reinstatement, a different tool for a different problem. A driver electing on an ordinary ticket wants the 4-hour BDI, and a course page pushing you toward a longer Florida course for a standard election deserves suspicion.

One clock clarification that relieves people: the famous 30-day deadline is for electing the course with the clerk, not completing it. Elect in time and the completion window runs on the clerk's schedule, with the course itself savable across sittings. Four hours against that window is the easy part; the election deadline is the part that bites.

Every approved online BDI course we track is compared on the Florida page, and the once-per-12-months, five-per-lifetime rationing is on our frequency page.

**Sources:** FLHSMV BDI/ADI | Fla. Stat. 318.14(9)

## How Much Does Traffic School Cost in Florida?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/florida/how-much-does-traffic-school-cost

- **Course price:** $5 to $25 for the 4-hour BDI across FLHSMV-approved schools we track
- **The catch:** Low headline prices often stack fees at checkout; compare final totals
- **The fine:** You still pay the civil penalty on the citation
- **Election deadline:** 30 days from the citation, with the clerk, before you pay or plead
- **Course length:** 4 hours (Basic Driver Improvement)
- **Certificate:** The school e-files with the clerk within 5 days (§318.1451), usually free; expedited options are upsells
- **What it buys:** Adjudication withheld, no points, and insurers can't raise your rate for it (§626.9541(1)(o))
- **Last verified:** August 2026

Florida runs the cheapest sticker prices in the country and the most creative checkouts. Both things are true, so here's how to read them.

The 4-hour BDI courses we track start at genuinely five dollars: 5DollarTrafficSchool at $5, Aceable currently at $5.94 against a $34.95 list, Improv at $23.95. Florida's market is a price war and drivers are the winners, mostly. The asterisk is the fee stack. Some low-headline schools add processing fees, certificate fees or "state fees" at checkout, so a $4.94 banner can leave the register at $30. The number that matters is the final total on the payment screen, and that's the number we compare schools on.

The course is also not the whole cost, and anyone telling you otherwise is selling something. You still pay the civil penalty on the ticket. What the election buys you is everything else: elect BDI with the clerk inside your 30-day window, finish the course, and adjudication is withheld, no points are assessed, and Florida law bars your insurer from raising your rate over that infraction. The fine you were always paying. The four-figure insurance exposure, roughly $3,966 over three years on a $204 ticket in our data as a ceiling estimate, is what the $5 course deletes.

Two pieces of follow-through. The election happens before you pay or plead, with the clerk of the county that issued the ticket, and missing the 30 days kills the option entirely. And once you finish, your school is required by law to e-file your certificate with the clerk within 5 days. That filing is included; paying extra for "rush certificate delivery" on a 4-hour online course is almost never necessary. Check the county's records portal that it landed and you're done.

## How Often Can You Take Traffic School in Florida?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/florida/how-often-can-you-take-traffic-school

- **Election frequency:** Once in any 12-month period
- **Lifetime cap:** 8 elections, total, ever (raised from five in 2025)
- **Deadline each time:** You must elect the course within 30 days of the citation
- **CDL holders:** Not eligible
- **Last verified:** August 2026

Florida runs two clocks, and it's the second one most drivers have never heard of.

The first clock is familiar: you can elect Basic Driver Improvement once in any 12-month period. The second is the one to respect: Florida caps you at eight elections in a lifetime, raised from five when the statute was amended in 2025 (s. 318.14(9)). Not eight per license cycle, not eight per decade. Eight, ever, tracked by the state across your driving life. Every election you spend in your twenties is one you don't have in your fifties.

That changes how to think about a marginal ticket. In most states the only question is whether the course is worth the tuition this time. In Florida there's a portfolio question stacked on top: is this ticket worth one of your remaining elections? A cheap ticket with minimal insurance consequence might not be, especially if you've already burned several. A ticket that would put real points on your record almost certainly is. Your election count is on your driving record; if you don't know your number, pull the record before deciding.

The deadline makes the decision urgent every time: you have 30 days from the citation to elect the course with the clerk. Miss it and that ticket's election never existed, no matter how many you have left.

The permanent rails don't move with frequency: CDL holders can't elect at all, and a citation for driving 30 mph or more over the limit is ineligible regardless of your count.

If you're electing, the full price stack is on our cost page, and every approved online BDI course we track is compared on the Florida page.

**Sources:** Fla. Stat. 318.14(9)

## Is Traffic School Worth It in Florida?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/florida/is-traffic-school-worth-it

- **Verdict:** Yes, with the most honest caveat in the series: Florida's return is the most modest of the big states
- **What you spend:** A low-priced course plus fees, typically $40 to $60 all-in beyond the ticket
- **What it can prevent:** Roughly $930 in three-year insurance exposure (ceiling estimate), up to roughly a 15 to 20x return
- **The rationing question:** Each use spends one of five lifetime elections
- **Last verified:** August 2026

Yes, but Florida deserves the honest version, because its numbers are different from its neighbors'.

Florida's insurance market punishes a single ticket less than most big states: our data shows a comparatively mild premium-increase percentage, putting three-year exposure on a typical ticket at roughly $930 as a ceiling estimate. The election route, paying the fine plus a 4-hour course and fees, typically costs $40 to $60 beyond the ticket itself, and buys no points, no conviction, and statutory protection against the surcharge, since Florida law bars insurers from raising rates on an election with no points. Up to roughly 15 to 20x on the money. Excellent by any normal standard, and still the smallest multiple among the big states on this site.

Why the modest multiple changes behavior: Florida is the state where the course competes with your lifetime ration. Five elections, ever. On a ticket whose realistic insurance consequence is small, especially for a driver whose carrier tapers or shrugs, spending election three of five is a real cost the sticker price doesn't show. Our rule of thumb: elect without hesitation when points would land on a record that matters, think twice on a marginal ticket late in your election count.

The clock either way: elect with the clerk within 30 days or the question answers itself.

Approved BDI courses are compared on the Florida page; the rationing math is on our frequency page.

**Sources:** Ticket Cost Study: https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket | 318.14(9) | 626.9541(1)(o)

## Can You Take Defensive Driving Online in Georgia?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/georgia/can-you-take-traffic-school-online

- **Online accepted:** Yes, for DDS-approved driver improvement courses
- **The credential:** Georgia DDS certification is what makes a course count for the 7-point reduction
- **The reduction isn't automatic:** You apply to DDS with your completion certificate
- **Court-ordered courses:** Follow the court's instructions on approved format
- **Last verified:** August 2026

Yes. Georgia's Department of Driver Services certifies driver improvement courses including online delivery, and a DDS-approved online course qualifies you for the state's headline benefit, the once-every-five-years reduction of up to 7 points.

The operative word is certified. Georgia's benefit is generous enough that the course market around it is noisy, and only DDS certification makes a certificate worth anything. Check the school's DDS approval before paying; every course we compare carries it.

Two process points that outrank the format question. First, the reduction isn't automatic: completing the course produces a certificate, and you apply to DDS with it. Course finished, application skipped, record unchanged. Second, if a court ordered or accepted a course as part of resolving your specific ticket, including Georgia's fine reductions of up to 20% and zero-point orders, the court's instructions control which courses and formats it accepts, so confirm with the clerk before enrolling for a court purpose.

Every DDS-approved online course we track is compared on the Georgia page, the five-year clock is on our frequency page, and pricing, roughly $20 to $95, is on our cost page.

**Sources:** OCGA 40-5-86 | DDS Court Reference Manual

## Does Defensive Driving Remove Points in Georgia?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/georgia/does-traffic-school-remove-points

- **Points removed:** Up to 7 points already on your record, not below zero
- **Legal basis:** O.C.G.A. §40-5-86; certificate submitted to the Department of Driver Services
- **Frequency:** Once in any 5-year period
- **How to claim:** Complete a DDS-certified Driver Improvement (defensive driving) course, then bring or mail the original certificate to DDS
- **Course length:** 6 hours; "Driver Improvement" and "Defensive Driving" are the same program
- **Suspension context:** Georgia suspends at 15 points in 24 months (drivers 21+); violations carry 2–6 points each
- **Court-side option:** If a court orders or accepts your certificate for a pending ticket, the base fine drops 20% and the court can dispose of it as a zero-point request
- **Insurance:** Premium discount on completion under O.C.G.A. §33-9-42
- **Last verified:** August 2026

Yes. Georgia is the one state where the question means exactly what it says and the answer is exactly yes.

Everywhere else this question needs a paragraph of translation. California masks, Texas dismisses, Florida withholds, New York adjusts the suspension math. Georgia reaches into your record and takes points off it. O.C.G.A. 40-5-86: complete a DDS-approved defensive driving course, submit your certificate to the Department of Driver Services, and your point total is reduced by seven points, down to but not below zero. Points that are already there, from tickets you already took the hit on. Once in any five-year period.

Claiming it is almost comically manual. You finish the 6-hour course, then you take the original certificate to a DDS customer service center, or mail it to the DDS in Conyers. The reduction doesn't happen on its own and your course provider doesn't do it for you. Finish the course, sit on the certificate, get nothing.

Context for what 7 points buys you. Georgia violations carry 2 to 6 points each and the state suspends an adult license at 15 points in a 24-month window. Seven points is two or three average tickets wiped from that count. If you're sitting at 10 or 12, this course is the difference between driving and not.

There's a second, less-known use for the same certificate, and it comes straight from the DDS's own reference manual for traffic court judges. If you have a ticket pending, a Georgia court can order you to a driver improvement clinic, or accept a completion certificate you bring in on your own. When it does either, the base fine is reduced by 20 percent and the court can dispose of the violation as a zero-point request, meaning the new ticket lands without points. Whether a judge plays it that way is the judge's call, it's discretionary, but the mechanism is printed in the state's own bench manual, and showing up to court with a completed certificate is the cheapest leverage available to a Georgia driver. The manual is also explicit that a court-side zero-point disposition and the DDS-side 7-point reduction can both happen inside the same five-year period. They're separate tools.

And the insurance angle stacks on top. Georgia law, O.C.G.A. 33-9-42, ties a premium discount to completing the course, about 10% on average in our data, roughly $250 a year on a typical Georgia premium. Courses run roughly $20 to $95 for the 6 hours depending on online versus classroom. Between the fine reduction, the point removal and the discount, Georgia has quietly built the most driver-friendly version of this program in the country, and almost nobody in Georgia knows all three pieces exist.

All of this is for Georgia licensees, though. Georgia doesn't assign points to [a driver licensed in another state](https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/out-of-state-ticket) in the first place, so for a visitor there's nothing for the 7-point reduction to remove — a quirk worth understanding before you enroll.

Every DDS-certified online course we track is compared on the Georgia page.

**Sources:** DDS Points and Points Reduction: https://dds.georgia.gov/georgia-licenseid/violations-suspensions-revocations/points-and-points-reduction | DDS Defensive Driving FAQ: https://dds.georgia.gov/defensive-driving-program-faqs | DDS Traffic Court Reference Manual: https://dds.georgia.gov/document/manual/court-reference-manual-2021-2022v3/download | O.C.G.A. 40-5-86, 33-9-42 | Ticket Cost Study: https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket

## How Long Is Defensive Driving in Georgia?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/georgia/how-long-does-traffic-school-take

- **Course length:** 6 hours for a DDS-certified driver improvement course
- **After the 6 hours:** The 7-point reduction still requires your application to DDS
- **Last verified:** August 2026

Six hours at any DDS-certified school, because Georgia's Department of Driver Services certifies courses to a standard length along with a standard curriculum. The school choice changes the price, roughly $20 to $95 across the market, and the experience; it can't change the clock.

Six hours is a meaningful sit, and Georgia attaches it to the country's biggest single prize, the reduction of up to 7 points, available once every five years, which is a fair trade and then some. Online delivery makes the hours schedulable: progress saves, and the realistic pattern is a couple of evenings.

The step people skip after hour six is the one that makes the hours count: the reduction isn't automatic on completion. You apply to DDS with your certificate, and until you do, your record sits exactly where it was. If a court sent you instead, the court's paperwork requirements control, and its deadline is the one to respect.

Every DDS-certified online course we track is compared on the Georgia page, the five-year clock is on our frequency page, and the pricing spread is on our cost page.

## How Much Does Defensive Driving Cost in Georgia?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/georgia/how-much-does-traffic-school-cost

- **Course price:** Roughly $20 to $30 online for the DDS-certified 6-hour course; classroom courses run higher, up to about $95
- **Fine reduction:** When a court orders or accepts your certificate for a pending ticket, the base fine drops 20%
- **Insurance:** Premium discount on completion under O.C.G.A. §33-9-42, about 10% on average
- **Points:** The same certificate claims the 7-point reduction from DDS, once every 5 years
- **Course length:** 6 hours; "Driver Improvement" and "Defensive Driving" are the same DDS program
- **Typical value:** One $25 course can return several hundred dollars across fine, points and premium
- **Last verified:** August 2026

Georgia's course costs about what lunch for two costs, and no state pays the certificate back harder.

The DDS-certified 6-hour course runs roughly $20 to $30 online, with I Drive Safely currently at $29. Classroom versions of the same program run higher, up to about $95, and buy you nothing extra: DDS treats Driver Improvement and Defensive Driving as one program, and the certificate is identical either way. Online is the same credential at a third of the price.

Now the part that makes Georgia unusual. That one certificate has three separate cash values, and most Georgia drivers only ever collect one of them.

Value one, the fine. If you have a ticket pending, Georgia courts can order you to a driver improvement clinic or accept a certificate you completed on your own, and when they do, the state's own reference manual for traffic court judges says the base fine is reduced by 20 percent. On a decent-sized ticket the fine reduction alone can cover the course.

Value two, the premium. O.C.G.A. 33-9-42 ties an insurance discount to completing the course, roughly 10% on average in our data, call it $250 a year on a typical Georgia premium. That's not a one-off. It's a rate reduction.

Value three, the points. The same certificate, submitted to DDS, removes up to 7 points already on your record under O.C.G.A. 40-5-86, once every five years. If you're carrying points, that's the piece that protects your license, and it's free once you've taken the course. You just have to actually bring or mail the original certificate to DDS, because nothing happens automatically.

So the honest cost answer for Georgia: about $25 out, and if you use all three values, several hundred dollars back in the first year. There isn't another state where the math tilts this far in the driver's favor.

## How Often Can You Take Defensive Driving in Georgia?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/georgia/how-often-can-you-take-traffic-school

- **For the 7-point reduction:** Once every 5 years
- **Court-ordered courses:** As often as courts order them; separate from the 5-year clock
- **Last verified:** August 2026

Once every five years, the longest wait in our coverage, attached to the biggest prize.

Georgia's deal under OCGA 40-5-86 is straightforward: complete an approved driver improvement course, apply to DDS, and up to 7 points come off your record. Seven points is more than most single violations put on, which is why Georgia guards it with a five-year interval where most states run one to three. Use it casually on a minor ticket and it's gone until the next presidential election cycle plus one.

So the Georgia question is always allocation. A 2-point ticket on an otherwise clean record barely dents you; Georgia suspends at 15 points in 24 months, and two points age off on their own. Spending the once-per-five-years reduction there is like using a fire extinguisher on a candle. The reduction earns its keep for drivers whose totals are genuinely climbing toward trouble, and for them it's the strongest single move any state offers.

Two things run outside the 5-year clock. Courts can order or accept a course as part of resolving a specific case as often as cases arise, including the fine reductions of up to 20% and zero-point orders Georgia courts can attach; those are per-case tools, not the DDS reduction, and using one doesn't spend your reduction. And under-21 drivers ordered to a course for certain offenses are in a mandatory lane with its own rules.

One process note that catches people: the reduction isn't automatic on course completion. You apply to DDS with your certificate. Finish the course and skip the application and your record doesn't move.

Pricing sits on our cost page, roughly $20 to $95 depending on school, and every approved online course we track is compared on the Georgia page.

## Is Defensive Driving Worth It in Georgia?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/georgia/is-traffic-school-worth-it

- **Verdict:** Yes when points are the problem; it is not an insurance shield
- **What you spend:** $20 to $95 and six hours
- **What it can do:** Up to 7 points off (once every 5 years), and courts can attach up to 20% fine reductions or zero-point orders
- **What it can't do:** Prevent the roughly $2,100 three-year insurance exposure (ceiling estimate) from a conviction insurers can see
- **Last verified:** August 2026

Yes, for the right problem. Georgia's course is a points tool, the strongest one in the country, and the mistake is expecting it to be an insurance tool too.

Start with what it does brilliantly. Up to 7 points off your record, once every five years, is a bigger single credit than any other state offers, and for a driver whose total is climbing toward Georgia's 15-points-in-24-months suspension line, a $20 to $95 course that resets most of the ladder is cheap at triple the price. Layer in what courts can attach when resolving a specific case, fine reductions up to 20% and zero-point orders, and the course earns its place in almost any Georgia ticket strategy where the court's open to it.

Now the honest limit. Georgia mandates no insurance discount for course completion, and the standard course doesn't erase the conviction; insurers see the ticket, and our data puts its three-year exposure at roughly $2,100 as a ceiling estimate on a typical citation. A zero-point order from a court can blunt some of that; the once-per-five-years reduction, taken later, doesn't reach back to hide anything. So the worth-it test is simple: if the question is your point total or a court's offer, yes, decisively. If the question is purely your premium, the course isn't the instrument, and nothing in Georgia quite is.

## Can You Take Defensive Driving Online in New Jersey?

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/new-jersey/can-you-take-traffic-school-online

- **Online accepted:** Yes. The standard 6-hour defensive driving course is MVC-approved for online delivery
- **What online earns:** The 2-point reduction and the mandated 5-10% insurance discount
- **The course you can't take online (or choose at all):** The 3-point Driver Improvement Program, classroom-only and MVC-initiated
- **Not eligible:** Commercial and out-of-state licenses
- **Last verified:** August 2026

Yes. New Jersey's standard defensive driving course, the 6-hour one behind the 2-point reduction and the mandated insurance discount, is MVC-approved for online delivery, and online is how most New Jerseyans take it.

The format confusion in New Jersey comes from there being two programs wearing similar names. The one you choose, the defensive driving course, is fully online-friendly. The one you don't, the Driver Improvement Program with its 3-point reduction, is classroom-only, and it's not a menu item anyway: the MVC initiates it for drivers at 12 to 14 points. If a website is selling you an online 3-point New Jersey course, it's selling something that doesn't exist.

Format changes nothing about the machinery: online completion still routes provider-to-MVC for the point credit, in 7 to 10 business days, with the MVC refusing driver-submitted certificates, and you still send your certificate to your insurer yourself for the discount. Commercial and out-of-state licenses stay excluded either way.
